title.zh: 卷八 梁本紀下第八 簡文帝 元帝 敬帝
title.en: Volume 8 :Liang Annals 3: Emperor Jianwen, Emperor Yuan, Emperor Jing
title.raw: 卷八 梁本紀下第八 簡文帝 元帝 敬帝 Volume 8 :Liang Annals 3: Emperor Jianwen, Emperor Yuan, Emperor Jing

sentences.zh: 梁本紀下第八

translations.literal: Liang Annals, Lower Fascicle Eight
translations.idiomatic: Liang Annals 3, Part Eight

sentences.zh: 太清三年，台城陷，太子坐永福省見侯景，神色自若，無懼容。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing, Taicheng fell; the Crown Prince sat in Yongfu Palace to receive Hou Jing, his expression composed, without a look of fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing, when Taicheng fell, the Crown Prince received Hou Jing in Yongfu Palace with perfect composure and not a trace of fear.

sentences.zh: 五月丙辰，帝崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingchen, the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingchen, the Emperor passed away.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，太子即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the Crown Prince ascended the imperial throne and proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the Crown Prince took the throne and issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸未，追尊穆貴嬪為皇太后，追諡妃王氏為簡皇后。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the late Consort Mu was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager, and Consort Wang was posthumously titled Empress Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the court posthumously honored the late Consort Mu as Empress Dowager and gave Consort Wang the posthumous title Empress Jian.

sentences.zh: 六月丙戌，以南康王會理為司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingxu, the Prince of Nankang, Hui-li, was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingxu, Prince Hui-li of Nankang was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，立宣城王大器為皇太子。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Prince of Xuancheng, Daqi, was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Prince Daqi of Xuancheng was installed as Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，立當陽公大心為尋陽郡王，石城公大款為江夏郡王，甯國公大臨為南海郡王，臨城公大連為南郡王，西豐公大春為安陸郡王，新淦公大成為山陽郡王，臨湘公大封為宜都郡王，高唐公大莊為新興郡王。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Duke of Dangyang, Daxin, was made Prince of Xunyang; the Duke of Shicheng, Dakuan, Prince of Jiangxia; the Duke of Ningguo, Dalin, Prince of Nanhai; the Duke of Lincheng, Dalian, Prince of Nan; the Duke of Xifeng, Dachun, Prince of Anlu; the Duke of Xingan, Dacheng, Prince of Shanyang; the Duke of Linxiang, Dafeng, Prince of Yidu; and the Duke of Gaotang, Dazhuang, Prince of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Da-xin, Duke of Dangyang, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xunyang; Da-kuan of Shicheng as Prince of Jiangxia; Da-lin of Ningguo as Prince of Nanhai; Da-lian of Lincheng as Prince of Nan; Da-chun of Xifeng as Prince of Anlu; Da-cheng of Xingan as Prince of Shanyang; Da-feng of Linxiang as Prince of Yidu; and Da-zhuang of Gaotang as Prince of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲寅，廣州刺史元景仲謀應侯景，西江督護陳霸先攻之，景仲自殺。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiayin, the Inspector of Guangzhou, Yuan Jingzhong, plotted to join Hou Jing; the Jiangxi Protector Chen Baxian attacked him, and Jingzhong killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiayin, Guangzhou Inspector Yuan Jingzhong plotted to side with Hou Jing. Chen Baxian, Protector of the West River route, attacked him, and Jingzhong took his own life.

sentences.zh: 霸先迎定州刺史蕭勃為刺史。

translations.literal: Baxian welcomed the Inspector of Dingzhou, Xiao Bo, to serve as Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Baxian then installed Xiao Bo, Inspector of Dingzhou, as the new Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以司空南康王會理為兼尚書令。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Minister of Works, the Prince of Nankang Hui-li, was additionally appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Minister of Works Prince Hui-li of Nankang was also named Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 是月，九江大饑，人相食者十四五。

translations.literal: That month, Jiujiang suffered a great famine; fourteen or fifteen out of ten people resorted to cannibalism.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jiujiang was stricken by famine so severe that perhaps one person in seven survived by eating the dead.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，征東大將軍、開府儀同三司、南徐州刺史蕭藻薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guimao, the General Who Conquers the East, Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry, and Inspector of South Xuzhou, Xiao Zao, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guimao, Xiao Zao—General Who Conquers the East, Commissioner with Grand Cavalry, and Inspector of South Xuzhou—died.

sentences.zh: 丙午，侯景矯詔：「儀同三司位比正公，自今悉不加將軍，以為定準。」

translations.literal: On bingwu, Hou Jing forged an edict: "Commissioners with the Third Rank are equal to full grandees; from now on the general title shall not be added to them, and this shall be the fixed standard."
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Hou Jing forged an edict declaring that holders of the Third Rank were equal to full grandees and that henceforth the general title would no longer be appended to such posts.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁未，地震。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on dingwei, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dingwei, the earth shook.

sentences.zh: 是月，百濟國遣使朝貢，見城寺荒蕪，哭于闕下。

translations.literal: That month, the kingdom of Baekje sent envoys with tribute; seeing the capital temples in ruins, they wept below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: That month envoys from Baekje arrived with tribute, and when they saw the capital temples lying waste they wept at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年春正月辛亥朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Dabao, on xinhai, the first day of the month, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Dabao, on xinhai, the first day of the first month, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，天雨黃沙。

translations.literal: On dingsi, yellow sand fell from the sky like rain.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi yellow sand rained from the sky.

sentences.zh: 己未，西魏克安陸，執司州刺史柳仲禮，盡有漢東地。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Western Wei captured Anlu and seized the Inspector of Sizhou, Liu Zhongli, taking all the lands east of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Western Wei took Anlu, captured Liu Zhongli, Inspector of Sizhou, and seized the entire Han River region.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，月晝見於東方。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the moon was visible in the east during the day.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the moon appeared in the eastern sky in daylight.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，前江都令祖皓起義兵於廣陵。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Zu Hao, former Magistrate of Jiangdu, raised a righteous army at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Zu Hao, former magistrate of Jiangdu, raised a loyalist force at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 二月癸未，侯景攻下廣陵，皓見害。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guiwei, Hou Jing captured Guangling and Hao was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guiwei, Hou Jing took Guangling and Hao was put to death.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以尚書僕射王克為左僕射。

translations.literal: On yisi, the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Wang Ke, was appointed Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Wang Ke, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was promoted to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 丙午，侯景逼帝幸西州。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Hou Jing compelled the Emperor to proceed to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Hou Jing forced the Emperor to visit Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子，前司州刺史羊鴉仁自尚書省出奔江陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengzi, the former Inspector of Sizhou, Yang Yaren, fled from the Masters of Writing office to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengzi, Yang Yaren, former Inspector of Sizhou, escaped from the Masters of Writing office and fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊辰，賊行台任約寇江州，刺史尋陽王大心以州降之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on wuchen, the rebel field officer Ren Yue raided Jiangzhou; the Inspector, the Prince of Xunyang Daxin, surrendered the province to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on wuchen, the rebel field officer Ren Yue invaded Jiangzhou, and Inspector Prince Da-xin of Xunyang surrendered the province.

sentences.zh: 八月甲午，湘東王繹遣領軍將軍王僧辯逼郢州，邵陵王綸棄郢州走。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu, the Prince of Xiangdong, Yi, sent the General of the Palace Guard Wang Sengbian to press Yingzhou; the Prince of Shaoling, Lun, abandoned Yingzhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiawu, Prince Yi of Xiangdong sent Wang Sengbian, General of the Palace Guard, to threaten Yingzhou, and Prince Lun of Shaoling abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 九月乙亥，侯景自進位相國，封二十郡為漢王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yihai, Hou Jing promoted himself to Chancellor and enfeoffed twenty commanderies as the kingdom of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yihai, Hou Jing elevated himself to Chancellor and created a kingdom of Han from twenty commanderies.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙未，景又逼帝幸西州曲宴，自加宇宙大將軍、都督六合諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on yiwei, Jing again compelled the Emperor to attend a banquet at Xizhou and added to himself the titles Grand General of the Cosmos and Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on yiwei, Jing again forced the Emperor to a banquet at Xizhou and took for himself the titles Grand General of the Cosmos and Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 立皇子大鈞為西陽郡王，大威為武甯郡王，大球為建安郡王，大昕為義安郡王，大摯為綏建郡王，大圜為樂梁郡王。

translations.literal: The imperial sons Dajun, Dawei, Daqiu, Daxin, Dazhi, and Dayuan were established as Princes of Xiyang, Wuning, Jian'an, Yi'an, Suijian, and Yueyang respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Da-jun was made Prince of Xiyang; Da-wei of Wuning; Da-qiu of Jian'an; Da-xin of Yi'an; Da-zhi of Suijian; and Da-yuan of Yueyang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，侯景害司空南康王會理。

translations.literal: On renyin, Hou Jing killed the Minister of Works, the Prince of Nankang Hui-li.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Hou Jing executed Minister of Works Prince Hui-li of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，任約進據西陽，分兵寇齊昌，執衡陽王獻送都下，害之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Ren Yue advanced and occupied Xiyang, sent detachments to raid Qichang, seized the Prince of Hengyang Xian, and sent him to the capital where he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Ren Yue seized Xiyang, sent columns to raid Qichang, captured Prince Xian of Hengyang, sent him to the capital, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹遣前甯州刺史徐文盛拒約，南郡王前中兵參軍張彪起義於會稽若邪山，攻破浙東諸縣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent the former Inspector of Ningzhou Xu Wensheng to resist Yue; the former Central Army Commander of Nan Commandery, Zhang Biao, raised a force on Ruoye Mountain in Kuaiji and overran the counties of eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Xiangdong dispatched former Ningzhou Inspector Xu Wensheng against Yue, while Zhang Biao, former Central Army Commander of Nan Commandery, raised troops on Ruoye Mountain in Kuaiji and swept through the counties of eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月，邵陵王綸走至安陸董城，為魏所攻，見殺。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring of the second year, the Prince of Shaoling Lun fled to Dongcheng in Anlu and was attacked and killed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the second year, Prince Lun of Shaoling fled to Dongcheng in Anlu, where Wei forces attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 三月庚戌，魏文帝崩。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengxu, Emperor Wen of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengxu, Emperor Wen of Wei passed away.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，侯景圍巴陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Hou Jing besieged Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Hou Jing laid siege to Baling.

sentences.zh: 六月乙巳，解圍宵遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yisi, he lifted the siege and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yisi, he broke off the siege and stole away under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，景還至建鄴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Jing returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Jing withdrew to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬寅，帝崩於永福省，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on renyin, the Emperor died in Yongfu Palace, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on renyin, the Emperor died in Yongfu Palace at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 賊偽諡曰明皇帝，廟稱高宗。

translations.literal: The rebels gave him the false posthumous title Bright Emperor and the temple name Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels posthumously styled him Emperor Ming with the temple name Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 明年三月己丑，王僧辯平侯景，率百官奉梓宮升廟堂。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, on jichou, Wang Sengbian suppressed Hou Jing and led the hundred officials to escort the imperial coffin into the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year, on jichou, Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing and led the court to install the imperial coffin in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 元帝追崇為簡文皇帝，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan posthumously honored him as Emperor Jianwen with the temple name Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan posthumously honored him as Emperor Jianwen with the temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 四月乙丑，葬莊陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on yichou, he was buried at Zhuang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on yichou, he was interred at Zhuang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝幼而聰睿，六歲便能屬文，武帝弗之信，於前面試，帝攬筆立成文。

translations.literal: The Emperor was clever and quick from childhood; at six he could compose prose, which Emperor Wu did not believe, so he tested him face to face and the Emperor took up the brush and completed an essay on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood the Emperor was bright and quick-witted; at six he could already compose prose. Emperor Wu doubted it and tested him in person, whereupon the boy took up the brush and finished an essay at once.

sentences.zh: 武帝歎曰：「常以東阿為虛，今則信矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sighed and said: "I always thought the tale of Cao Zhi was empty talk; now I must believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sighed and said, "I always thought the story of Cao Zhi was mere legend; now I see it is true.

sentences.zh: 」及長，器宇寬弘，未嘗見喜慍色，尊嚴若神。

translations.literal: "When he grew up, his bearing was broad and generous; he was never seen to show joy or anger, and his dignity was like that of a god.
translations.idiomatic: "As he matured his manner was open and magnanimous; he never showed pleasure or displeasure on his face, and his dignity seemed almost superhuman.

sentences.zh: 方頤豐下，須鬢如畫，直發委地，雙眉翠色。

translations.literal: His face was full below broad brows; his beard and sideburns were like a painting; his straight hair reached the ground; his two eyebrows were jade-green.
translations.idiomatic: He had a broad forehead and full lower face, a beard and side-whiskers like a painted portrait, hair that fell straight to the ground, and eyebrows of vivid green.

sentences.zh: 項毛左旋，連錢入背。

translations.literal: The hair at the nape of his neck curled leftward, linking in coin-like patterns into his back.
translations.idiomatic: The hair at the nape of his neck curled to the left in linked coin-shaped whorls that ran down his back.

sentences.zh: 手執玉如意，不相分辨。

translations.literal: He held a jade ruyi scepter, indistinguishable from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: In his hand he held a jade ruyi scepter so perfectly matched to his grip that hand and scepter seemed one.

sentences.zh: 眄睞則目光燭人。

translations.literal: When he glanced sideways, the light of his eyes could illuminate a person.
translations.idiomatic: A sidelong glance from his eyes seemed to cast light upon whoever he looked at.

sentences.zh: 讀書十行俱下，辭藻豔發，博綜群言，善談玄理。

translations.literal: He read ten lines at a glance; his literary style was brilliant; he mastered all schools of thought and was skilled at discussing Neo-Daoist principles.
translations.idiomatic: He could read ten lines at once, wrote in a brilliant style, mastered every school of learning, and excelled at Neo-Daoist discourse.

sentences.zh: 自十一便能親庶務，曆試藩政，所在稱美。

translations.literal: From eleven he could personally handle routine affairs; tested repeatedly in frontier administration, wherever he served he won praise.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of eleven he could manage affairs himself; after repeated trials in frontier posts, he was praised wherever he governed.

sentences.zh: 性恭孝，居穆貴嬪憂，哀毀骨立，所坐席沾濕盡爛。

translations.literal: His nature was reverent and filial; during mourning for Consort Mu he was so emaciated that only bones remained, and the mat he sat on was soaked through and rotted away.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and reverent by nature, in mourning for Consort Mu he wasted away until little more than bone remained, and the mat beneath him rotted from constant weeping.

sentences.zh: 在襄陽拜表侵魏，遣長史柳津、司馬董當門、壯武將軍杜懷寶、振遠將軍曹義宗等進軍克南陽、新野等都，拓地千餘里。

translations.literal: While at Xiangyang he submitted a memorial invading Wei and sent the Chief Clerk Liu Jin, Marshal Dong Dangmen, the General Who Displays Martial Prowess Du Huaibao, the General Who Shakes Distant Foes Cao Yizong, and others to advance and capture Nanyang, Xinye, and other prefectures, extending territory more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he memorialized the throne to strike Wei and dispatched Chief Clerk Liu Jin, Marshal Dong Dangmen, General Who Displays Martial Prowess Du Huaibao, General Who Shakes Distant Foes Cao Yizong, and others to advance, capturing Nanyang, Xinye, and other prefectures and extending Liang territory by more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 及居監撫，多所弘宥，文案簿領，纖豪必察。

translations.literal: When he held the post of Supervisor and Regent he showed much clemency, yet in documents and ledgers he scrutinized even the smallest detail.
translations.idiomatic: As Supervisor and Regent he was broadly lenient in policy, yet in paperwork and accounts he examined even the smallest item.

sentences.zh: 弘納文學之士，賞接無倦。

translations.literal: He welcomed literary men and rewarded and received them without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered literary men around him and entertained them with inexhaustible generosity.

sentences.zh: 嘗于玄圃述武帝所制五經講疏，聽者傾朝野。

translations.literal: Once in the Mystic Garden he expounded the commentaries on the Five Classics composed by Emperor Wu, and listeners filled court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the Mystic Garden he lectured on Emperor Wu's commentaries to the Five Classics, and the audience filled both court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 雅好賦詩，其自序云：「七歲有詩癖，長而不倦。

translations.literal: He dearly loved composing poetry; in his own preface he wrote: "At seven I had a passion for verse, and I have never tired of it.
translations.idiomatic: He loved writing poetry; in his own preface he wrote, "At seven I was already obsessed with verse, and I have never outgrown it.

sentences.zh: 」然帝文傷於輕靡，時號「宮體」。

translations.literal: "Yet the Emperor's writing tended toward the frivolous and decadent, and at the time it was called the "Palace Style."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet his prose leaned toward the frivolous and decadent, and contemporaries called it the Palace Style.

sentences.zh: 所著昭明太子傳五卷，諸王傳三十卷，禮大義二十卷，長春義記一百卷，法寶連璧三百卷，謝客文涇渭三卷，玉簡五十卷，光明符十二卷，易林十七卷，灶經二卷，沐浴經三卷，馬槊譜一卷，棋品五卷，彈棋譜一卷，新增白澤圖五卷，如意方十卷，文集一百卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: His works included a Biography of Crown Prince Zhaoming in five juan, Biographies of the Princes in thirty juan, Great Principles of Ritual in twenty juan, Record of Righteousness of Eternal Spring in one hundred juan, Treasures Linked Like Jade in three hundred juan, Discriminating the Waters of Xie's Writings in three juan, Jade Slips in fifty juan, Talismans of Bright Light in twelve juan, Forest of Changes in seventeen juan, Classic of the Hearth in two juan, Classic of Bathing in three juan, Treatise on the Horse Spear in one juan, Grades of Go in five juan, Treatise on Pop Go in one juan, Newly Expanded White Ze Illustrations in five juan, Recipe of the Ruyi in ten juan, and a Collected Works in one hundred juan—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Among his published works were a Biography of Crown Prince Zhaoming in five juan, Biographies of the Princes in thirty juan, Great Principles of Ritual in twenty juan, Record of Righteousness of Eternal Spring in one hundred juan, Treasures Linked Like Jade in three hundred juan, Discriminating the Waters of Xie's Writings in three juan, Jade Slips in fifty juan, Talismans of Bright Light in twelve juan, Forest of Changes in seventeen juan, Classic of the Hearth in two juan, Classic of Bathing in three juan, Treatise on the Horse Spear in one juan, Grades of Go in five juan, Treatise on Pop Go in one juan, Newly Expanded White Ze Illustrations in five juan, Recipe of the Ruyi in ten juan, and Collected Works in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 初，景納帝女溧陽公主，公主有美色，景惑之，妨于政事，王偉每以為言，景以告主，主出惡言。

translations.literal: At first Jing took in marriage the Emperor's daughter, the Princess of Liyang; the princess was beautiful, and Jing was infatuated with her to the detriment of state affairs; Wang Wei often remonstrated, and Jing told the princess, who spoke harshly in reply.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hou Jing married the Emperor's daughter, the Princess of Liyang. She was beautiful, and his infatuation with her began to interfere with government; Wang Wei repeatedly remonstrated, and Jing told the princess, who answered with bitter words.

sentences.zh: 偉知之，懼見讒，乃謀廢帝而後間主。

translations.literal: When Wei learned of this he feared slander and therefore plotted to depose the Emperor and then estrange the princess.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei learned of this he feared being slandered and plotted to depose the Emperor and then turn the princess against him.

sentences.zh: 苦勸行殺，以絕眾心。

translations.literal: He urged execution strenuously, to cut off the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed hard for the Emperor's death to extinguish all loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 廢後，王偉乃與彭雋、王修纂進觴於帝曰：「丞相以陛下幽憂既久，使臣上壽。

translations.literal: After the deposition, Wang Wei together with Peng Juan and Wang Xiuzuan came forward with cups and said to the Emperor: "The Chancellor, seeing Your Majesty long confined in sorrow, has sent us to offer birthday wine."
translations.idiomatic: After the deposition Wang Wei came forward with Peng Juan and Wang Xiuzuan, cups in hand, and said, "The Chancellor, seeing you long confined in grief, has sent us to offer birthday wine."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「已禪帝位，何得言陛下？

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "I have already abdicated the throne—how can you still say 'Your Majesty'?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor smiled and said, "I have already abdicated—how can you still call me 'Your Majesty'?

sentences.zh: 此壽酒將不盡此乎。

translations.literal: Will this birthday wine not be the last I drink?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this birthday wine not meant to be my last?"

sentences.zh: 」於是雋等並齎酒肴、曲項琵琶，與帝極飲。

translations.literal: Thereupon Juan and the others all brought wine and food and curved-neck pipa, and drank with the Emperor to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Then Juan and the others brought wine, food, and curved-neck pipas, and drank with the Emperor until utterly sated.

sentences.zh: 帝知將見殺，乃盡酣，謂曰：「不圖為樂，一至於斯。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew he was about to be killed and therefore drank his fill, saying: "I never imagined pleasure could come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he was about to die, the Emperor drank himself into oblivion and said, "I never thought merriment could end like this."

sentences.zh: 」既醉而寢，偉乃出，雋進土囊，王修纂坐上，乃崩。

translations.literal: When he was drunk and asleep, Wei went out; Juan brought in a bag of earth, Wang Xiuzuan sat upon him, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When he had drunk himself unconscious, Wei withdrew; Juan brought in a bag of earth, Wang Xiuzuan sat on the Emperor's chest, and he died.

sentences.zh: 竟協於夢。

translations.literal: It accorded entirely with a dream he had had.
translations.idiomatic: The manner of his death matched a dream he had once had.

sentences.zh: 偉撤戶扉為棺，遷殯於城北酒庫中。

translations.literal: Wei removed the door panels for a coffin and moved the body for temporary burial to a wine storehouse north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stripped door panels to make a coffin and moved the body for temporary burial to a wine storehouse north of the city.

sentences.zh: 帝自幽縶之後，賊乃撤內外侍衛，使突騎圍守，牆垣悉有枳棘。

translations.literal: After the Emperor was confined, the rebels removed inner and outer guards and had mounted raiders surround and hold him; the walls were all planted with thorn hedges.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Emperor was imprisoned the rebels removed all inner and outer guards, posted mounted raiders to hold him, and planted thorn hedges along every wall.

sentences.zh: 無復紙，乃書壁及板鄣為文。

translations.literal: There was no paper left, so he wrote on walls and board partitions.
translations.idiomatic: With no paper available he wrote on walls and wooden partitions instead.

sentences.zh: 自序云：「有梁正士蘭陵蕭世贊，立身行道，終始若一，風雨如晦，雞鳴不已。

translations.literal: In his own preface he wrote: "There is a upright gentleman of Liang, Xiao Shizan of Lanling, who in establishing himself and walking the Way was one from beginning to end; through wind and rain as at dusk, the cock crows unceasingly.
translations.idiomatic: In one preface he wrote, "There is an upright gentleman of Liang, Xiao Shizan of Lanling, who from first to last walked the Way without wavering; through wind and rain at twilight the cock still crows.

sentences.zh: 弗欺暗室，豈況三光？

translations.literal: He does not deceive even in a dark room—how much less under the three luminaries?
translations.idiomatic: He does not deceive even in a dark room—how much less beneath sun, moon, and stars?

sentences.zh: 數至於此，命也如何！

translations.literal: To come to this pass so many times—such is fate; what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: To reach this pass again and again is fate; what can one do!

sentences.zh: 」又為文數百篇。

translations.literal: He also composed several hundred more pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote several hundred additional pieces.

sentences.zh: 崩後，王偉觀之，惡其辭切，即使刮去。

translations.literal: After his death Wang Wei read them, hated their cutting tone, and had them scraped away.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Wang Wei read these writings, loathed their biting tone, and had them scraped from the walls.

sentences.zh: 有隨偉入者，誦其連珠三首，詩四篇，絕句五篇，文並悽愴云。

translations.literal: Someone who entered with Wei recited from memory three linked-pearl pieces, four poems, five quatrains, and other writings—all poignant in tone.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who entered with Wei recited from memory three linked-pearl compositions, four poems, five quatrains, and other pieces—all heartbreakingly poignant.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝元皇帝諱繹，字世誠，小字七符，武帝第七子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoyuan, the Shizu, was named Yi, courtesy name Shicheng, childhood name Qifu; he was the seventh son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoyuan, temple name Shizu, was named Yi, courtesy name Shicheng, childhood name Qifu, and was the seventh son of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝夢眇目僧執香爐，稱托生王宮。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu dreamed of a one-eyed monk holding an incense burner, saying he would be reborn in the royal palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once dreamed of a one-eyed monk holding an incense burner who declared he would be reborn in the palace.

sentences.zh: 既而帝母在采女次侍，始褰戶幔，有風回裾，武帝意感幸之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Emperor's mother, while attending among the palace women, first lifted the door curtain; a wind caught her skirt, and Emperor Wu was moved and favored her.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, while the Emperor's mother was serving among the palace women, she lifted a door curtain and a gust caught her skirt; Emperor Wu was stirred and took her to his bed.

sentences.zh: 采女夢月墮懷中，遂孕。

translations.literal: The palace woman dreamed the moon fell into her bosom, and thereafter she conceived.
translations.idiomatic: The woman dreamed the moon fell into her bosom, and she conceived.

sentences.zh: 天監七年八月丁巳生帝，舉室中非常香，有紫胞之異。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianjian, eighth month, on dingsi, the Emperor was born; throughout the chamber there was an extraordinary fragrance, and there was the marvel of a purple afterbirth.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianjian, eighth month, on dingsi, the Emperor was born; the room filled with an unearthly fragrance, and the afterbirth was purple.

sentences.zh: 武帝奇之，因賜采女姓阮，進為修容。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu marveled at this and therefore granted the palace woman the surname Ruan and promoted her to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was astonished, granted the woman the surname Ruan, and promoted her to the rank of Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 十三年，封湘東王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，累遷為鎮西將軍、都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was promoted in succession to General Who Pacifies the West, Commander-in-Chief, and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing he rose in succession to General Who Pacifies the West, Commander-in-Chief, and Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，侯景陷建鄴。

translations.literal: In the third year, third month, Hou Jing captured Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, third month, Hou Jing took Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 四月，世子方等至自建鄴，知台城不守。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the heir Fangdeng arrived from Jiankang and learned that Taicheng could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the heir Fangdeng arrived from Jiankang with word that Taicheng could not be held.

sentences.zh: 帝命柵江陵城，周回七十里。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered palisades built around Jiangling city, seventy li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince ordered Jiangling fortified with palisades encircling the city for seventy li.

sentences.zh: 鎮西長史王沖等拜箋請為太尉、都督中外諸軍事，承制主盟。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk of the Pacifying West headquarters, Wang Chong, and others submitted a memorial requesting that he be made Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief of Inner and Outer Forces, and assume provisional authority as covenant leader.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wang Chong and others of the Pacifying West headquarters submitted a memorial asking him to become Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief of Inner and Outer Forces, and provisional covenant leader.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，曰：「吾於天下不賤，甯俟都督之名；

translations.literal: The Emperor did not consent and said: "I am not lowly in the realm—why should I wait for the title of commander-in-chief?
translations.idiomatic: He refused, saying, "I am not insignificant in the realm—why should I wait for the title of commander-in-chief?

sentences.zh: 帝子之尊，何藉上臺之位。

translations.literal: The dignity of an emperor's son—what need is there to borrow the position of the high platform?
translations.idiomatic: As an imperial son, what need have I of the high platform's rank?

sentences.zh: 議者可斬。

translations.literal: Whoever urges this may be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever urges this may be executed."

sentences.zh: 」投筆流淚。

translations.literal: He cast down his brush and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He threw down his brush and wept.

sentences.zh: 沖等重請，不從。

translations.literal: Chong and the others pressed again, but he would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and the others pressed again, but he would not agree.

sentences.zh: 又請為司空，以主諸侯，亦弗聽。

translations.literal: They again requested that he be Minister of Works to preside over the feudal lords, but he likewise would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: They then asked that he accept the Ministry of Works to oversee the feudal lords, but he again refused.

sentences.zh: 乃開鎮西府，辟天下士。

translations.literal: He then opened the Pacifying West headquarters and recruited men of talent throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened the Pacifying West headquarters and recruited talent from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝徵兵于湘州刺史河東王譽，譽拒命。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor summoned troops from the Inspector of Xiangzhou, the Prince of Hedong Yu, and Yu disobeyed the order.
translations.idiomatic: That month he summoned troops from Xiangzhou Inspector Prince Yu of Hedong, but Yu disobeyed.

sentences.zh: 尋上甲侯韶自建鄴至，宣三月十五日密詔，授帝位假黃鉞、大都督中外諸軍事、司徒、承制。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter the armored envoy Hou Shao arrived from Jiankang, proclaiming the secret edict of the fifteenth day of the third month, granting the Emperor the provisional use of the yellow battle-axe, Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief of Inner and Outer Forces, Minister of Works, and provisional imperial authority.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the armored envoy Hou Shao arrived from Jiankang bearing the secret edict of the fifteenth day of the third month, granting provisional use of the yellow battle-axe, the titles Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief of Inner and Outer Forces, and Minister of Works, and provisional imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 於是立行台于南郡而置官司焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established a field headquarters at Nan Commandery and set up official posts.
translations.idiomatic: He then established a field headquarters at Nan Commandery and appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 七月，遣世子方等討河東王譽，軍敗，死之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he sent the heir Fangdeng to campaign against the Prince of Hedong Yu; the army was defeated and Fangdeng died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he sent the heir Fangdeng against Prince Yu of Hedong; the army was defeated and Fangdeng was killed.

sentences.zh: 又遣鎮兵將軍鮑泉討譽。

translations.literal: He again sent the General Who Garrisons the Army Bao Quan to campaign against Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent General Who Garrisons the Army Bao Quan against Yu.

sentences.zh: 九月乙卯，雍州刺史岳陽王察舉兵寇江陵，其將杜崱兄弟來降，察遁走。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yimao, the Inspector of Yongzhou, the Prince of Yueyang Cha, raised troops and invaded Jiangling; his generals the Du brothers came over in surrender, and Cha fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yimao, Yongzhou Inspector Prince Cha of Yueyang raised troops and invaded Jiangling; his generals the Du brothers defected, and Cha fled.

sentences.zh: 鮑泉攻湘州，未克；

translations.literal: Bao Quan attacked Xiangzhou but could not capture it;
translations.idiomatic: Bao Quan attacked Xiangzhou but failed to take it;

sentences.zh: 又遣左衛將軍王僧辯代將。

translations.literal: he again sent the General of the Left Guard Wang Sengbian to replace him as commander.
translations.idiomatic: he then sent General of the Left Guard Wang Sengbian to replace him.

sentences.zh: 及簡文帝即位，改元為大寶元年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne, the reign era was changed to the first year of Dabao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne the era name was changed to Dabao.

sentences.zh: 帝以簡文制於賊臣，卒不遵用。

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing Jianwen controlled by rebel ministers, ultimately did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince, seeing Jianwen controlled by rebel ministers, refused to adopt the new era name.

sentences.zh: 正月，使少子方晷質于魏，魏不受質而結為兄弟。

translations.literal: In the first month he sent his youngest son Fanggui as hostage to Wei; Wei would not accept the hostage but instead entered into brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month he sent his youngest son Fanggui to Wei as a hostage; Wei declined the hostage but entered into a pact of brotherhood instead.

sentences.zh: 四月，克湘州，斬譽，湘州平。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Xiangzhou was captured, Yu was executed, and Xiangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Xiangzhou fell, Yu was executed, and the province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史岳陽王察自稱梁王，蕃于魏，魏遣兵助伐襄陽。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yongzhou, the Prince of Yueyang Cha, declared himself King of Liang and submitted to Wei; Wei sent troops to help attack Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou Inspector Prince Cha of Yueyang declared himself King of Liang, submitted to Wei, and Wei sent troops to help him attack Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，邵陵王綸書已言凶事，秘之，以待湘州之捷。

translations.literal: Earlier, a letter from the Prince of Shaoling Lun had already reported the calamity, but it was kept secret pending victory in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Lun of Shaoling had already sent word of the disaster, but the Prince kept it secret while awaiting victory in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是月壬寅，始命陳瑩報武帝崩問，帝哭於正寢。

translations.literal: That month, on renyin, he finally ordered Chen Ying to announce the mourning news of Emperor Wu's death; the Emperor wept in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: That month, on renyin, he finally ordered Chen Ying to announce Emperor Wu's death; the Prince wept in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 六月，江夏王大款、山陽王大成、宜都王大封自信安來奔。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Princes of Jiangxia Dakuan, Shanyang Dacheng, and Yidu Dafeng fled from Xin'an to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Princes Da-kuan of Jiangxia, Da-cheng of Shanyang, and Da-feng of Yidu fled from Xin'an to join him.

sentences.zh: 九月辛酉，以前郢州刺史南平王恪為中衛將軍、尚書令、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinyou, the former Inspector of Yingzhou, the Prince of Nanping Ke, was appointed General of the Central Guard, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinyou, former Yingzhou Inspector Prince Ke of Nanping was named General of the Central Guard, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Commissioner with Grand Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 改封大款為臨川郡王，大成為桂陽郡王，大封為汝南郡王。

translations.literal: Dakuan was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan, Dacheng as Prince of Guiyang, and Dafeng as Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Da-kuan was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Linchuan, Da-cheng as Prince of Guiyang, and Da-feng as Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲子，南平王恪等奉箋進位相國，總百揆。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, Prince Ke of Nanping and others submitted a memorial urging him to the rank of Chancellor and overall governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiazi, Prince Ke of Nanping and others submitted a memorial urging him to accept the chancellorship and overall governance.

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，侯景悉兵西上。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Hou Jing mustered all his troops and marched west.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year Hou Jing marched west with his full army.

sentences.zh: 四月，景遣其將宋子仙、任約襲郢州，執刺史方諸。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Jing sent his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to raid Yingzhou and seized the Inspector Fang Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Jing sent his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to raid Yingzhou and captured Inspector Fang Zhu.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，領軍王僧辯屯師巴陵。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the General of the Palace Guard Wang Sengbian encamped his army at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Wang Sengbian, General of the Palace Guard, encamped at Baling.

sentences.zh: 五月癸未，帝遣將胡僧佑、陸法和援巴陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guiwei, the Emperor sent the generals Hu Sengyou and Lu Fahé to relieve Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guiwei, he sent Generals Hu Sengyou and Lu Fahé to relieve Baling.

sentences.zh: 六月，僧佑等擊破景將任約軍，禽約，景解圍宵遁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Sengyou and the others defeated the army of Jing's general Ren Yue, captured Yue, and Jing lifted the siege and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Sengyou and the others routed Ren Yue, captured him, and Jing broke off the siege and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 以王僧辯為征東將軍、開府儀同三司、尚書令，帥眾追景，所至皆捷。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian was appointed General Who Conquers the East, Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry, and Director of the Masters of Writing, and led the host in pursuit of Jing; wherever he went he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian was made General Who Conquers the East, Commissioner with Grand Cavalry, and Director of the Masters of Writing, and pursued Jing with success at every turn.

sentences.zh: 進圍郢州，獲賊將宋子仙等。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Yingzhou and captured the rebel generals Song Zixian and others.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to besiege Yingzhou and captured rebel generals including Song Zixian.

sentences.zh: 九月，盤盤國獻馴象。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the kingdom of Panpan presented tame elephants.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the kingdom of Panpan presented tame elephants as tribute.

sentences.zh: 十月辛丑朔，紫雲如蓋臨江陵城。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on xinchou, the first day of the month, purple clouds like a canopy hovered over Jiangling city.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on xinchou, the first day of the month, purple clouds like a canopy gathered over Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 是月，簡文帝崩，開府儀同三司王僧辯等奉表勸進。

translations.literal: That month Emperor Jianwen died; Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry Wang Sengbian and others submitted a memorial urging accession.
translations.idiomatic: That month Emperor Jianwen died, and Wang Sengbian, Commissioner with Grand Cavalry, and others submitted a memorial urging accession.

sentences.zh: 帝奉諱，大臨三日，百官縞素，答表不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor observed mourning, wailing greatly for three days; the hundred officials wore white hemp; he replied to the memorial refusing.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning and wailed for three days; the officials wore white hemp; he answered the memorial with refusal.

sentences.zh: 司空南平王恪率宗室，領軍將軍胡僧佑率群僚，江州別駕張佚率吏人，並奉箋勸進。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works, Prince Ke of Nanping, led the imperial clan; the General of the Palace Guard Hu Sengyou led the officials; the Aide of Jiangzhou Zhang Yi led the clerks and people—all submitting memorials urging accession.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Prince Ke of Nanping led the imperial clan, General of the Palace Guard Hu Sengyou led the officials, and Jiangzhou Aide Zhang Yi led the clerks and people—all urging accession.

sentences.zh: 帝固讓。

translations.literal: The Emperor firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙亥，僧辯又奉表勸進，又不從。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yihai, Sengbian again submitted a memorial urging accession, and again he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yihai, Sengbian again urged accession, and again he refused.

sentences.zh: 時巨寇尚存，帝未欲即位，而四方表勸，前後相屬，乃下令斷表。

translations.literal: At that time the great rebel still survived; the Emperor did not yet wish to ascend the throne, yet memorials urging him came from all quarters in succession, so he issued an order cutting off further submissions.
translations.idiomatic: The great rebel still lived and he did not yet wish to take the throne, yet urging memorials poured in from every quarter, so he ordered them stopped.

sentences.zh: 承聖元年二月，王僧辯眾軍發自尋陽，帝馳檄四方，購獲景及逆者，封萬戶開國公，絹布五萬疋。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengsheng, second month, Wang Sengbian's combined armies set out from Xunyang; the Emperor issued proclamations to the four quarters, offering a reward of ten thousand households and a founding marquisate, plus fifty thousand bolts of silk and cloth, for capturing Jing and other rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Chengsheng, Wang Sengbian's combined armies set out from Xunyang; the Prince issued proclamations throughout the realm offering ten thousand households, a founding marquisate, and fifty thousand bolts of silk and cloth for the capture of Jing and other rebels.

sentences.zh: 三月，僧辯等平景，傳首江陵。

translations.literal: In the third month Sengbian and the others suppressed Jing and sent his head to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Sengbian and the others defeated Jing and sent his head to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以賊平告明堂、太社。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the suppression of the rebels was announced at the Bright Hall and the Altar of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi victory over the rebels was announced at the Bright Hall and the Altar of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 己丑，僧辯等又表勸進曰：

translations.literal: On jichou, Sengbian and the others again submitted a memorial urging accession, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Sengbian and the others again submitted a memorial urging accession, saying:

sentences.zh: 眾軍以今月戊子，總集建康，賊景鳥伏獸窮，頻擊頻挫，奸竭詐盡，深溝自固。

translations.literal: The armies on this day, wuzi, assembled at Jiankang; the rebel Jing, like a bird in hiding and a beast at bay, was struck again and again and repeatedly broken; his treachery exhausted and his deceit spent, he dug deep moats and held himself fast.
translations.idiomatic: "On this day, wuzi, our armies assembled at Jiankang. The rebel Jing, cornered like a hunted bird and a trapped beast, was struck again and again until his treachery was spent; he dug deep moats and held himself fast.

sentences.zh: 臣等分勒武旅，百道同趨，突騎短兵，犀函鐵楯，結隊千群，持戟百萬，止紂七步，圍項三重，轟然大潰，群凶四滅。

translations.literal: Your ministers divided and commanded martial hosts; a hundred routes advanced together; raiding cavalry and short weapons, rhinoceros-hide shields and iron pavises, formed ranks by the thousand and held halberds by the million; stopping within seven paces of Zhou, encircling Xiang in three rings, they burst asunder with a thunderous crash and the evil host was extinguished on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: We divided our forces and marched by a hundred routes; raiding cavalry and short weapons, rhinoceros-hide shields and iron pavises, ranks by the thousand and halberds by the million closed within seven paces as at Zhou and encircled in three rings as at Xiang; with a thunderous crash the evil host was shattered on every side.

sentences.zh: 京師少長，俱稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Young and old of the capital all cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Young and old in the capital all cried, "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 長安酒食，于此價高。

translations.literal: Wine and food in Chang'an—here the price is high.
translations.idiomatic: Wine and food in Chang'an—here the price is high indeed.

sentences.zh: 九縣雲開，六合清朗，矧伊黔首，誰不載躍。

translations.literal: The nine districts open like clouds; the six directions are clear and bright—how much more the common people, who would not leap for joy?
translations.idiomatic: The nine districts open like parting clouds; the six directions grow bright—how much more the common people, who leap for joy!

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下咀痛茹哀，嬰憤忍酷。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty chews grief and swallows sorrow, bears infant rage and endures cruel wrong.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly consider that Your Majesty chews grief and swallows sorrow, bearing rage like an infant and enduring cruel wrong.

sentences.zh: 自紫庭絳闕，胡塵四起，壖垣好畤，冀馬雲屯，泣血臨兵，嘗膽誓眾。

translations.literal: Since the crimson court and cinnabar gate, dust of the barbarians rose on four sides; ramparts and good earthworks, Ji horses clouded in mass; with blood in the eyes he led troops and tasted gall to swear the host.
translations.idiomatic: Since the crimson court and cinnabar gate, barbarian dust rose on four sides; ramparts and good earthworks, Ji horses massed like clouds; with blood in his eyes he led troops and tasted gall to bind the host by oath.

sentences.zh: 而吳、楚一家，方與七國俱反，管、蔡流言，又以三監作亂。

translations.literal: Yet Wu and Chu were one family, and together with the Seven States they rebelled; Guan and Cai spread slander, and again the Three Overseers raised disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu and Chu were one family and rose with the Seven States; Guan and Cai spread slander and the Three Overseers again raised disorder.

sentences.zh: 西涼義眾，阻秦塞而不通，并州遺黎，跨飛狐而見絕。

translations.literal: Righteous hosts of Western Liang were blocked at the Qin passes and could not pass through; remnant people of Bingzhou, crossing Flying Fox, were cut off from sight.
translations.idiomatic: Righteous hosts of Western Liang were blocked at the Qin passes; remnant people of Bingzhou, crossing Flying Fox, were cut off from contact.

sentences.zh: 豺狼當路，非止一人，鯨鯢不梟，倏焉五載。

translations.literal: Wolves and jackals blocked the road—not just one man; great whales and crocodiles were not beheaded, and suddenly five years passed.
translations.idiomatic: Wolves and jackals blocked the road—not one alone; great whales went unbeheaded, and five years passed in a flash.

sentences.zh: 英武克振，怨恥並雪，永尋霜露，伊何可勝。

translations.literal: Heroic martial spirit was restored; grievance and shame were both wiped away; forever seeking frost and dew—how can it be borne?
translations.idiomatic: Heroic martial spirit revived; grievance and shame were wiped away; forever seeking frost and dew upon the tombs—how can sorrow be borne?

sentences.zh: 臣等輒依故實，奉修社廟，使者持節，分告園陵。

translations.literal: Your ministers have accordingly followed old precedent, reverently repaired the altars of soil and grain, sent envoys bearing insignia, and separately announced the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers have accordingly followed old precedent, reverently repaired the altars of soil and grain, sent envoys bearing insignia, and separately announced the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 嗣後升遐，龍輴未殯，承華掩曜，梓宮莫測。

translations.literal: The late Emperor ascended to the far realm; the dragon carriage is not yet interred; the splendor of the Eastern Palace is veiled; the imperial coffin cannot be located.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor has ascended to the far realm; the dragon carriage is not yet interred; the splendor of the Eastern Palace is veiled; the imperial coffin cannot be found.

sentences.zh: 並即隨由備辦，禮具凶荒，四海同哀，六軍袒哭。

translations.literal: All were immediately prepared accordingly; ritual implements in time of calamity; the four seas mourn together; the six armies bared their shoulders and wept.
translations.idiomatic: All were immediately prepared as required; ritual implements in a time of calamity; the four seas mourn together; the six armies bared their shoulders and wept.

sentences.zh: 聖情孝友，理當感慟。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sacred feeling of filial piety and brotherly love should rightly be deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sacred filial piety and brotherly love should rightly move you to deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 日者，百司嶽牧，仰祈宸鑒，以錫珪之功，既歸有道，當璧之禮，允屬聖明。

translations.literal: Recently the hundred offices and prefects looked up seeking the imperial mirror, that the merit of granting the jade scepter might return to the one who holds the Way; the rite of receiving the jade disk should rightly belong to the sage and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the hundred offices and prefects looked up seeking the imperial mirror, that the merit of granting the jade scepter might return to the one who holds the Way; the rite of receiving the jade disk should belong to the sage and bright.

sentences.zh: 而優詔謙沖，杳然凝邈，飛龍可躋，而幹爻在四，帝閽雲叫，而閶闔未開。

translations.literal: Yet Your gracious edict was modest and restrained, remote and distant; the flying dragon could be ascended, yet the Qian line remained in the fourth place; the imperial gate cried out like clouds, yet the great gate was not opened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your gracious edict was modest and restrained, remote and distant; the flying dragon could be mounted, yet the Qian line remained in the fourth place; the imperial gate cried out like clouds, yet the great gate was not opened.

sentences.zh: 謳歌再馳，是用翹首。

translations.literal: Song again galloped forth—therefore we raise our heads in hope.
translations.idiomatic: Song again galloped forth—therefore we raise our heads in hope.

sentences.zh: 所以越人固執，熏丹穴以求君，周人樂推，踰岐山而事主。

translations.literal: Therefore the people of Yue stubbornly held fast, fumigating the cinnabar cave to seek a lord; the people of Zhou gladly pushed forward, crossing Mount Qi to serve their master.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the people of Yue stubbornly held fast, fumigating the cinnabar cave to seek a lord; the people of Zhou gladly pushed forward, crossing Mount Qi to serve their master.

sentences.zh: 漢王不即位，無以貴功臣，光武止蕭王，豈謂紹宗廟。

translations.literal: If the King of Han did not ascend the throne, he could not honor meritorious ministers; if Emperor Guangwu stopped the King of Xiao, how could he continue the ancestral temple?
translations.idiomatic: If the King of Han did not ascend the throne he could not honor meritorious ministers; if Emperor Guangwu stopped the King of Xiao, how could he continue the ancestral temple?

sentences.zh: 黃帝游於襄城，尚訪御人之道，放勳寂于姑射，猶使鐏俎有歸。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor wandered at Xiangcheng yet still inquired about the Way of ruling men; Emperor Yao was silent at Guniu yet still made the sacrificial vessels have their place.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor wandered at Xiangcheng yet still inquired about the Way of ruling men; Emperor Yao was silent at Guniu yet still ensured the sacrificial vessels had their place.

sentences.zh: 伊此儻來，豈聖人所欲，帝王所應，不獲已而然。

translations.literal: That such things come by chance is surely not what the sage desires; what emperors and kings should do—they act thus because they cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: That such things come by chance is surely not what the sage desires; emperors and kings act thus only because they cannot do otherwise.

sentences.zh: 伏讀璽書，尋諷制旨，領懷物外，未奉慈衷。

translations.literal: We humbly read the imperial seal letter and sought the meaning of the edict; holding the realm beyond the body, we have not yet received the compassionate heart.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly read the imperial seal letter and sought the meaning of the edict; holding the realm beyond the body, we have not yet received the compassionate heart.

sentences.zh: 陛下日角龍顏之姿，表于徇齊之日，彤雲素靈之瑞，基於應物之初。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sun-horn and dragon-countenance appeared on the day of uniform yielding; auspicious crimson clouds and white numen took root from the beginning of responding to things.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sun-horn and dragon-countenance appeared on the day of uniform yielding; auspicious crimson clouds and white numen took root from the beginning of responding to things.

sentences.zh: 博學則大哉無所與名，深言則曄乎文章之觀。

translations.literal: In learning, great indeed—there is none with whom to share the name; in profound speech, brilliant is the vista of literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: In learning he is so great that none may share the name; in profound speech the vista of literary accomplishment shines.

sentences.zh: 忠為令德，孝實動天。

translations.literal: Loyalty is the fine virtue; filial piety truly moves Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty is the fine virtue; filial piety truly moves Heaven.

sentences.zh: 加以英威茂略，雄圖武算，指麾則丹浦不戰，顧眄則阪泉自蕩。

translations.literal: Added to this are heroic authority and abundant strategy, bold design and martial calculation; at a gesture Danpu does not fight; at a glance Mount Banquan clears itself.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this are heroic authority and abundant strategy, bold design and martial calculation; at a gesture Danpu does not fight; at a glance Mount Banquan clears itself.

sentences.zh: 地維絕而重紐，天柱傾而更植。

translations.literal: The earth's cords broke and were reknotted; the pillar of Heaven tilted and was replanted.
translations.idiomatic: The earth's cords broke and were reknotted; the pillar of Heaven tilted and was replanted.

sentences.zh: 鑿河津于孟門，百川復啟；

translations.literal: The river ford was cut open at Meng Gate; the hundred streams flowed again;
translations.idiomatic: The river ford was cut open at Meng Gate; the hundred streams flowed again;

sentences.zh: 補穹儀以五石，萬物再生。

translations.literal: the round heaven was mended with five stones; the ten thousand things were reborn.
translations.idiomatic: the round heaven was mended with five stones; the ten thousand things were reborn.

sentences.zh: 縱陛下拂袗衣而游廣成，登龕山而去東土，群臣安得仰訴，兆庶何所歸仁。

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty shook out the plain robe and wandered at Guangcheng, ascended Mount Kan and departed the eastern lands—how could your ministers raise their appeal, and to whom would the multitude turn for benevolence?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty shook out the plain robe and wandered at Guangcheng, ascended Mount Kan and departed the eastern lands—how could your ministers raise their appeal, and to whom would the multitude turn for benevolence?

sentences.zh: 況郊祀配天，罍篚禮曠，齋宮清廟，匏竹不陳。

translations.literal: Moreover, in suburban sacrifice matching Heaven, the wine vessels and baskets stand empty; in the pure palace and clear temple, gourd pipes and bamboo pipes are not displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in suburban sacrifice matching Heaven the wine vessels and baskets stand empty; in the pure palace and clear temple, gourd pipes and bamboo pipes are not displayed.

sentences.zh: 仰望鸞輿，匪朝伊夕，瞻言法駕，載渴且饑。

translations.literal: Gazing up at the imperial carriage—not one morning or evening; looking to the law chariot—thirsty and hungry together.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing up at the imperial carriage—not one morning or evening; looking to the law chariot—thirsty and hungry together.

sentences.zh: 豈可久稽眾議，有曠彝則。

translations.literal: How can the multitude's deliberations be long delayed, and the constant law be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: How can the multitude's deliberation be long delayed and the constant law neglected?

sentences.zh: 舊邦凱復，函、洛已平，高奴、櫟陽，宮館雖毀；

translations.literal: The old capital is restored in triumph; Hangu and Luoyang are already pacified; Gaonu and Liyang—the palaces and halls though ruined;
translations.idiomatic: The old capital is restored in triumph; Hangu and Luoyang are already pacified; Gaonu and Liyang—the palaces and halls though ruined;

sentences.zh: 濁河清渭，佳氣猶存。

translations.literal: the muddy Yellow River and clear Wei still preserve their auspicious vapors.
translations.idiomatic: the muddy Yellow River and clear Wei still preserve their auspicious vapors.

sentences.zh: 皋門有伉，甘泉四敞，土圭測景，仙人承露。

translations.literal: The outer gate has its pillars; Sweet Spring is open on four sides; the earth ruler measures the shadow; immortals receive the dew.
translations.idiomatic: The outer gate has its pillars; Sweet Spring is open on four sides; the earth ruler measures the shadow; immortals receive the dew.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋九州之赤縣，六合之樞機。

translations.literal: This is the red district of the Nine Provinces, the pivot of the Six Directions.
translations.idiomatic: This is the red district of the Nine Provinces, the pivot of the Six Directions.

sentences.zh: 博士捧圖書而稍還，太常定禮儀其已立，豈得不揚清警而赴名都，具玉鑾而旋正寢。

translations.literal: Doctors of learning carry books and gradually return; the Director of Ritual has already established ceremonies—how can you not sound the clear alarm and go to the famous capital, prepare the jade chariot and return to the proper palace?
translations.idiomatic: Doctors of learning carry books and gradually return; the Director of Ritual has already established ceremonies—how can you not sound the clear alarm and go to the famous capital, prepare the jade chariot and return to the proper palace?

sentences.zh: 昔東周既遷，鎬京遂其不復，長安一亂，郟、洛永以為居。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Eastern Zhou moved, Haojing was never restored; after one disorder in Chang'an, Jia and Luo were forever the seat.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when the Eastern Zhou moved, Haojing was never restored; after one disorder in Chang'an, Jia and Luo were forever the seat.

sentences.zh: 夏後以萬國朝諸侯，文王以六州匡天下，方之跡基百里，劍仗三尺，以殘楚之地，抗拒六戎，一旅之卒，翦夷三叛，坦然大定，禦輦東歸。

translations.literal: Yu of Xia had the myriad states attend the feudal lords; King Wen with six provinces corrected all under Heaven—compared with a foundation of a hundred li and swords and staffs of three feet, using the remnant lands of Chu to resist the six Rong, with troops of one brigade cutting down three rebellions, calmly settling the great order and driving the imperial carriage east—
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia had the myriad states attend the feudal lords; King Wen with six provinces corrected all under Heaven—compared with a foundation of a hundred li and swords and staffs of three feet, using the remnant lands of Chu to resist the six Rong, with troops of one brigade cutting down three rebellions, calmly settling the great order and driving the imperial carriage east—

sentences.zh: 解五牛于冀州，秣六馬於譙郡，緬求前古，其可得歟？

translations.literal: unhitching five oxen at Jizhou, feeding six horses at Qiao Commandery—seeking this in former antiquity, can it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: unhitching five oxen at Jizhou, feeding six horses at Qiao Commandery—seeking this in former antiquity, can it be obtained?

sentences.zh: 對揚天命，無所讓德，有理存焉，敢重祈奏。

translations.literal: In response to Heaven's mandate there is no virtue to yield; reason exists herein—we dare again earnestly memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: In response to Heaven's mandate there is no virtue to yield; reason exists herein—we dare again earnestly memorialize.

sentences.zh: 帝尚未從。

translations.literal: The Emperor had still not consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince had still not consented.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，宣猛將軍朱買臣奉帝密旨，害豫章王棟及其二弟橋、樛。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the General Who Proclaims Fierceness Zhu Maichen, bearing the Emperor's secret order, killed the Prince of Yuzhang Dong and his two younger brothers Qiao and Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao General Who Proclaims Fierceness Zhu Maichen, bearing the secret order, killed Prince Dong of Yuzhang and his two younger brothers Qiao and Jiao.

sentences.zh: 四月乙巳，益州刺史、新除假黃鉞、太尉武陵王紀僭位於蜀，年號天正。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, on yisi, the Inspector of Yizhou, the newly appointed provisional bearer of the yellow battle-axe and Grand Commandant, the Prince of Wuling Ji, usurped the throne in Shu with the era name Tianzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on yisi, Yizhou Inspector and newly appointed provisional bearer of the yellow battle-axe and Grand Commandant Prince Ji of Wuling usurped the throne in Shu under the era name Tianzheng.

sentences.zh: 帝遣兼司空蕭泰、祠部尚書樂子雲拜謁塋陵，修復社廟。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the Concurrent Minister of Works Xiao Tai and the Director of Sacrifices Yue Ziyun to pay respects at the imperial tombs and restore the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Concurrent Minister of Works Xiao Tai and Director of Sacrifices Yue Ziyun to pay respects at the imperial tombs and restore the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，下令解嚴。

translations.literal: On dingsi, he issued an order lifting the martial law.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he issued an order lifting martial law.

sentences.zh: 五月庚午，司空南平王恪及宗室王侯、大都督王僧辯等，復拜表上尊號。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengwu, the Minister of Works Prince Ke of Nanping together with the imperial clan princes and marquises, the Grand Commandant Wang Sengbian, and others again submitted a memorial offering the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengwu, Minister of Works Prince Ke of Nanping together with the imperial clan, Grand Commandant Wang Sengbian, and others again submitted a memorial offering the exalted title.

sentences.zh: 帝猶固讓。

translations.literal: The Emperor still firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He still firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以開府儀同三司、江州刺史王僧辯為司徒。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry and Inspector of Jiangzhou Wang Sengbian was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Wang Sengbian, Commissioner with Grand Cavalry and Inspector of Jiangzhou, was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，斬賊左僕射王偉、尚書呂季略、少府卿周石珍、舍人嚴亶於江陵市，乃下令赦境內。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the rebel Left Vice Director Wang Wei, Director of the Masters of Writing Lü Jilüe, Director of the Palace Storehouse Zhou Shizhen, and Attendant Yan Dan were executed in the Jiangling market; he then issued an order granting amnesty within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou rebel Left Vice Director Wang Wei, Director of the Masters of Writing Lü Jilüe, Director of the Palace Storehouse Zhou Shizhen, and Attendant Yan Dan were executed in the Jiangling market; he then proclaimed amnesty within the borders.

sentences.zh: 齊將潘樂、辛術等攻秦郡，王僧辯遣將杜崱帥眾拒之。

translations.literal: The Qi generals Pan Yue and Xin Shu and others attacked Qin Commandery; Wang Sengbian sent the general Du Yan to command troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi generals Pan Yue and Xin Shu attacked Qin Commandery; Wang Sengbian sent General Du Yan to resist them.

sentences.zh: 以陳霸先為征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Baxian was appointed General Who Conquers the North, Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian was made General Who Conquers the North, Commissioner with Grand Cavalry, and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊人賀平侯景。

translations.literal: The people of Qi congratulated the pacification of Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qi congratulated the defeat of Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 八月，武陵王紀率巴、蜀之眾東下，遣護軍將軍陸法和屯巴峽以拒之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Prince of Wuling Ji led the hosts of Ba and Shu eastward; he sent the Protector of the Army Lu Fahé to encamp at Baxia to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Prince Ji of Wuling led the hosts of Ba and Shu eastward; he sent Protector of the Army Lu Fahé to encamp at Baxia to resist them.

sentences.zh: 九月甲戌，司空南平王恪薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiaxu, the Minister of Works Prince Ke of Nanping died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiaxu, Minister of Works Prince Ke of Nanping died.

sentences.zh: 十月乙未，前梁州刺史蕭循自魏至江陵，以為平北將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on yiwei, the former Inspector of Liangzhou Xiao Xun came from Wei to Jiangling and was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on yiwei, former Liangzhou Inspector Xiao Xun came from Wei to Jiangling and was made General Who Pacifies the North and Commissioner with Grand Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 戊申，執湘州刺史王琳于殿內。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Inspector of Xiangzhou Wang Lin was seized inside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Xiangzhou Inspector Wang Lin was seized inside the hall.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，琳長史陸納及其將潘烏累等舉兵反，攻陷湘州。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Lin's Chief Clerk Lu Na and his generals Pan Wulei and others raised troops in revolt and captured Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Lin's Chief Clerk Lu Na and his generals Pan Wulei and others rebelled and captured Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是月，四方征鎮王公卿士復勸進表，三上，乃許之。

translations.literal: That month, the lords, ministers, and officials of the four quarters again submitted memorials urging accession; after three submissions he consented.
translations.idiomatic: That month lords, ministers, and officials from the four quarters again urged accession; after three submissions he consented.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏廢帝元年。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of the deposed Emperor of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the first year of the deposed Emperor of Wei.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月乙丑，詔王僧辯討陸納。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month, on yichou, an edict ordered Wang Sengbian to campaign against Lu Na.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month, on yichou, an edict ordered Wang Sengbian to campaign against Lu Na.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以吏部尚書王褒為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Bao was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Wang Bao, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 己卯，江夏宮南門鑰牡飛。

translations.literal: On jimao, the lock bolt of the south gate of the Jiangxia Palace flew out.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the lock bolt of the south gate of the Jiangxia Palace flew out.

sentences.zh: 三月庚寅，有兩龍見湘州西江。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengyin, two dragons appeared in the West River of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengyin, two dragons appeared in the West River of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏五月甲申，魏大將尉遲迥進兵逼巴西，潼州刺史楊幹運以城納迥。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, on jiashen, the Grand General of Wei Yuwen Jiong advanced troops pressing Baxi; the Inspector of Tongzhou Yang Ganyun surrendered the city to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on jiashen, Wei Grand General Yuwen Jiong advanced against Baxi; Tongzhou Inspector Yang Ganyun surrendered the city to him.

sentences.zh: 己丑，武陵王紀軍至西陵。

translations.literal: On jichou, the army of the Prince of Wuling Ji reached Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the army of Prince Ji of Wuling reached Xiling.

sentences.zh: 六月乙卯，王僧辯平湘州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yimao, Wang Sengbian pacified Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yimao, Wang Sengbian pacified Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，武陵王紀眾大潰，見殺。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, the host of the Prince of Wuling Ji was utterly routed and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the army of Prince Ji of Wuling was utterly routed and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 八月戊戌，尉遲迥平蜀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuxu, Yuwen Jiong pacified Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuxu, Yuwen Jiong pacified Shu.

sentences.zh: 九月，齊遣郭元建及將邢杲遠、步大汗薩、東方老帥眾頓合肥。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Qi sent Guo Yuanjian and the generals Xing Xiaoyuan, Bu Dahan Sa, and Dongfang Lao to command troops encamped at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Qi sent Guo Yuanjian and generals Xing Xiaoyuan, Bu Dahan Sa, and Dongfang Lao to encamp at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月辛酉，僧辯留鎮姑孰，豫州刺史侯瑱據東關壘，征吳興太守裴之橫帥眾繼之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on xinyou, Sengbian remained to garrison Gushu; the Inspector of Yuzhou Hou Tian occupied the fortress at Dongguan, and the Administrator of Wuxing Pei Zhiheng led troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, on xinyou, Sengbian remained to garrison Gushu; Yuzhou Inspector Hou Tian held the fortress at Dongguan, and Wuxing Administrator Pei Zhiheng led troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以尚書右僕射王褒為左僕射，湘東太守張綰為右僕射。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Bao was appointed Left Vice Director, and the Administrator of Xiangdong Zhang Wan was appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Wang Bao was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Xiangdong Administrator Zhang Wan was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 十二月，宿預土人東方光據城歸化，齊江西州郡皆起兵應之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the native of Suyu Dongfang Guang occupied the city and submitted; Qi commanderies west of the river all raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Dongfang Guang of Suyu occupied the city and submitted; Qi commanderies west of the river all rose in response.

sentences.zh: 三月，主衣庫見黑蛇長丈許，數十小蛇隨之，舉頭高丈餘南望，俄失所在。

translations.literal: In the third month, in the wardrobe store a black serpent more than a zhang long was seen, followed by several dozen small serpents; it raised its head more than a zhang high facing south, then suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month a black serpent more than a zhang long was seen in the wardrobe store, followed by dozens of smaller serpents; it raised its head more than a zhang high facing south, then suddenly vanished.

sentences.zh: 帝又與宮人幸玄洲苑，復見大蛇盤屈於前，群小蛇遶之，並黑色。

translations.literal: The Emperor again visited the Mystic Islet Garden with palace women and again saw a great serpent coiled before them; a swarm of small serpents encircled it—all black.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again visited the Mystic Islet Garden with palace women and saw a great serpent coiled before them, encircled by a swarm of small serpents—all black.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，宮人曰：「此非怪也，恐是錢龍。

translations.literal: The Emperor hated this; a palace woman said: "This is no portent—perhaps it is a Money Dragon."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was troubled; a palace woman said, "This is no omen—perhaps it is a Money Dragon."

sentences.zh: 」帝敕所司即日取數千萬錢鎮於蛇處以厭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the office concerned that very day to take tens of millions in cash and bury it at the serpent's place to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the office concerned that very day to bury tens of millions in cash where the serpent had appeared to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 因設法會，赦囚徒，振窮乏，退居棲心省。

translations.literal: He then held a Buddhist assembly, pardoned prisoners, relieved the destitute, and withdrew to dwell in the Rest-the-Heart Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a Buddhist assembly, pardoned prisoners, relieved the destitute, and withdrew to the Rest-the-Heart Palace.

sentences.zh: 又有蛇從屋墮落帝帽上，忽然便失。

translations.literal: Again a serpent fell from the roof onto the Emperor's hat and suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Again a serpent fell from the roof onto the Emperor's hat and suddenly vanished.

sentences.zh: 又龍光殿上所禦肩輿復見小蛇縈屈輿中，以頭駕夾膝前金龍頭上，見人走去，逐之不及。

translations.literal: Again on the imperial shoulder carriage in Longguang Hall a small serpent was seen coiled in the carriage, its head resting on the golden dragon head before the knees; seeing people it fled, and though pursued it could not be caught.
translations.idiomatic: Again on the imperial shoulder carriage in Longguang Hall a small serpent was seen coiled in the carriage, its head resting on the golden dragon head before the knees; seeing people it fled and could not be caught.

sentences.zh: 城濠中龍騰出，煥爛五色，竦躍入雲，六七小龍相隨飛去。

translations.literal: In the city moat a dragon leapt out, brilliant in five colors, soaring into the clouds; six or seven small dragons followed and flew away.
translations.idiomatic: In the city moat a dragon leapt out in brilliant five colors and soared into the clouds; six or seven small dragons followed and flew away.

sentences.zh: 群魚騰躍，墜死于陸道。

translations.literal: Shoals of fish leapt and fell dead on the land road.
translations.idiomatic: Shoals of fish leapt from the water and fell dead on the land road.

sentences.zh: 龍處為窟若數百斛圌。

translations.literal: Where the dragon had been became a lair like a granary of several hundred hu.
translations.idiomatic: Where the dragon had been a lair opened like a granary of several hundred hu.

sentences.zh: 舊大城上常有紫氣，至是稍復消歇。

translations.literal: Formerly on the great wall there had often been purple vapor; by this time it gradually faded away.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly purple vapor had often appeared on the great wall; by this time it gradually faded away.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以司徒王僧辯為太尉、車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Minister of Works Wang Sengbian was appointed Grand Commandant and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Minister of Works Wang Sengbian was made Grand Commandant and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以護軍將軍、郢州刺史陸法和為司徒。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Protector of the Army and Inspector of Yingzhou Lu Fahé was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Protector of the Army and Yingzhou Inspector Lu Fahé was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸酉，以征北大將軍、開府儀同三司陳霸先為司空。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on guiyou, General Who Conquers the North and Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry Chen Baxian was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on guiyou, General Who Conquers the North and Commissioner with Grand Cavalry Chen Baxian was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未，有黑氣如龍見於殿內。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guiwei, black vapor like a dragon appeared inside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guiwei, black vapor like a dragon appeared inside the hall.

sentences.zh: 秋九月辛卯，帝于龍光殿述老子義。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinmao, the Emperor expounded the meaning of Laozi in Longguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinmao, the Emperor expounded the meaning of Laozi in Longguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏使宇文仁恕來聘，齊使又至江陵，帝接仁恕有闕，魏相安定公憾焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei sent Yuwen Renshu as envoy; Qi also sent envoys to Jiangling; the Emperor's reception of Renshu was deficient, and the Wei Chancellor the Duke of Anding resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei had sent Yuwen Renshu as envoy and Qi also sent envoys to Jiangling; the Emperor's reception of Renshu was deficient, and Wei Chancellor the Duke of Anding resented this.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，使柱國萬紐於謹來攻。

translations.literal: On yisi, he sent the Pillar of State Yuwen Niyu to attack.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he sent Pillar of State Yuwen Niyu to attack.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙寅，魏軍至襄陽，梁王蕭察率眾會之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on bingyin, Wei troops reached Xiangyang; the King of Liang Xiao Cha led troops to join them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on bingyin, Wei troops reached Xiangyang; King of Liang Xiao Cha led troops to join them.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，停講，內外戒嚴，輿駕出行城柵，大風拔木。

translations.literal: On dingmao, lectures were suspended; inner and outer quarters were placed on alert; the imperial carriage went out to the city palisades; a great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao lectures were suspended; inner and outer quarters were placed on alert; the imperial carriage went out to the city palisades; a great wind uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 丙子，續講，百僚戎服以聽。

translations.literal: On bingzi, lectures resumed; the hundred officials listened in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi lectures resumed; the hundred officials listened in military dress.

sentences.zh: 詔征王僧辯。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Wang Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Wang Sengbian.
