sentences.zh: 十一月甲申，幸津陽門講武，置南北兩城主。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiashen, he visited Jinyang Gate to review troops and appointed lords for the southern and northern walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiashen, he visited Jinyang Gate to review troops and appointed lords for the southern and northern walls.

sentences.zh: 帝親觀閱，風雨總集，部分未交，旗幟飄亂，帝趣駕而回，無復次序。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally inspected them; wind and rain gathered together; the formations were not yet set when banners and flags were blown into disorder; the Emperor hurried the carriage back and all order was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally inspected them; wind and rain gathered together; before formations were set banners and flags were blown into disorder; the Emperor hurried the carriage back and all order was lost.

sentences.zh: 風雨隨息，眾竊驚焉。

translations.literal: When wind and rain ceased the crowd secretly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: When wind and rain ceased the crowd secretly marveled.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以領軍胡僧佑為都督城東城北諸軍事，右僕射張綰為副；

translations.literal: On yiyou, the General of the Palace Guard Hu Sengyou was made Commander-in-Chief of the eastern and northern city sectors, with Right Vice Director Zhang Wan as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou General of the Palace Guard Hu Sengyou was made Commander-in-Chief of the eastern and northern city sectors, with Right Vice Director Zhang Wan as deputy;

sentences.zh: 左僕射王褒都督城西城南諸軍事，直殿省元景亮為副。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Bao commanded the western and southern city sectors, with Yuan Jingliang of the Direct Attendance Office as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Bao commanded the western and southern sectors, with Yuan Jingliang of the Direct Attendance Office as deputy.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏軍至柵下。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Wei troops reached below the palisades.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Wei troops reached below the palisades.

sentences.zh: 丙申，征廣州刺史王琳入援。

translations.literal: On bingshen, an edict summoned Guangzhou Inspector Wang Lin to enter and relieve the siege.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen an edict summoned Guangzhou Inspector Wang Lin to enter and relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，大風，城內火燒居人數千家。

translations.literal: On dingyou, a great wind; fire in the city burned the dwellings of several thousand families.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou a great wind blew; fire in the city burned the dwellings of several thousand families.

sentences.zh: 以為失在婦人，斬首屍之。

translations.literal: It was thought the fault lay with women; heads were cut off and the corpses displayed.
translations.idiomatic: It was thought the fault lay with women; heads were cut off and the corpses displayed.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝猶賦詩無廢。

translations.literal: That day the Emperor still composed poetry without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Emperor still composed poetry without interruption.

sentences.zh: 以胡僧佑為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Hu Sengyou was appointed Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sengyou was appointed Commissioner with Grand Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 庚子，信州刺史徐世譜、晉安王司馬任約軍次馬頭岸。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Inspector of Xinzhou Xu Shipu and the Chief Clerk of the Prince of Jin'an Ren Yue encamped at Matou Bank.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Xinzhou Inspector Xu Shipu and Chief Clerk of the Prince of Jin'an Ren Yue encamped at Matou Bank.

sentences.zh: 是夜，有流星墜城中，帝援蓍筮之，卦成，取龜式驗之，因抵於地曰：「吾若死此下，豈非命乎？

translations.literal: That night a falling star dropped into the city; the Emperor took up yarrow stalks to divinate; when the hexagram was complete he took the tortoise mold to verify it, then struck it to the ground and said: "If I am to die here, is it not fate?
translations.idiomatic: That night a falling star dropped into the city; the Emperor divined with yarrow stalks; when the hexagram was complete he verified it with the tortoise mold, then struck it to the ground and said, "If I am to die here, is it not fate?

sentences.zh: 」因裂帛為書催僧辯曰：「吾忍死待公，可以至矣。

translations.literal: "He then tore silk into a letter urging Sengbian: "I endure death waiting for you—you may come now."
translations.idiomatic: "He then tore silk into a letter urging Sengbian: "I endure death waiting for you—you may come now."

sentences.zh: 」戊申，胡僧佑、朱買臣等出戰，買臣敗績。

translations.literal: On wushen, Hu Sengyou, Zhu Maichen, and others went out to battle; Maichen was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Hu Sengyou, Zhu Maichen, and others went out to battle; Maichen was defeated.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏軍大攻，帝出枇杷門親臨陣督戰。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Wei troops launched a great attack; the Emperor went out through the Pipa Gate to personally oversee the battle from the front.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Wei troops launched a great attack; the Emperor went out through the Pipa Gate to personally oversee the battle from the front.

sentences.zh: 僧佑中流矢薨，軍敗，反者斬西門守卒以納魏軍。

translations.literal: Sengyou was struck by a flying arrow and died; the army was defeated; rebels cut down the western gate guards to admit Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou was struck by a flying arrow and died; the army was defeated; rebels cut down the western gate guards to admit Wei troops.

sentences.zh: 帝見執，如梁王蕭察營，甚見詰辱。

translations.literal: The Emperor was seized and taken to the camp of the King of Liang Xiao Cha, where he was greatly insulted and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was seized and taken to the camp of King of Liang Xiao Cha, where he was grossly insulted and interrogated.

sentences.zh: 他日，乃見魏僕射長孫儉，譎儉云：「埋金千斤於城內，欲以相贈。

translations.literal: Another day he was brought before the Wei Vice Director Changsun Qian; he deceived Qian, saying: "A thousand jin of gold is buried inside the city—I wish to give it to you."
translations.idiomatic: Another day he was brought before Wei Vice Director Changsun Qian and deceived him, saying, "A thousand jin of gold is buried inside the city—I wish to give it to you."

sentences.zh: 」儉乃將帝入城，帝因述察相辱狀，謂儉曰：「向聊相譎，欲言耳；

translations.literal: Qian therefore led the Emperor into the city; the Emperor then described Cha's insults and said to Qian: "I was merely jesting to speak—
translations.idiomatic: Qian therefore led the Emperor into the city; the Emperor then described Cha's insults and said to Qian, "I was merely jesting to speak—

sentences.zh: 豈有天子自埋金乎？

translations.literal: would an emperor bury gold himself?"
translations.idiomatic: would an emperor bury gold himself?"

sentences.zh: 」儉乃留帝於主衣庫。

translations.literal: Qian therefore detained the Emperor in the wardrobe store.
translations.idiomatic: Qian therefore detained the Emperor in the wardrobe store.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙辰，徐世譜、任約退戍巴陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingchen, Xu Shipu and Ren Yue withdrew to garrison Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingchen, Xu Shipu and Ren Yue withdrew to garrison Baling.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏人戕帝。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Wei men killed the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Wei men killed the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，梁王方智承制，追尊為元皇帝，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year, the King of Liang Fangzhi assumed provisional authority and posthumously honored him as Emperor Yuan with the temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year King of Liang Fangzhi assumed provisional authority and posthumously honored him as Emperor Yuan with the temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 帝聰悟俊朗，天才英發，出言為論，音響若鍾。

translations.literal: The Emperor was clever, perceptive, handsome, and bright; his heavenly talent flourished brilliantly; when he spoke it became discourse, and the sound was like a bell.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was clever, perceptive, handsome, and bright; his talent flourished brilliantly; when he spoke it became discourse, and his voice rang like a bell.

sentences.zh: 年五六歲，武帝嘗問所讀書，對曰：「能誦曲禮。

translations.literal: At five or six years of age, Emperor Wu once asked what books he was reading; he answered: "I can recite the Record of Rites."
translations.idiomatic: At five or six Emperor Wu once asked what books he was reading; he answered, "I can recite the Record of Rites."

sentences.zh: 」武帝使誦之，即誦上篇。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had him recite it, and he recited the first section.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had him recite it, and he recited the first section.

sentences.zh: 左右莫不驚歎。

translations.literal: Those around him were all startled and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him were all startled and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 初生患眼，醫療必增，武帝自下意療之，遂盲一目。

translations.literal: At birth he suffered from eye disease; medical treatment always worsened it; Emperor Wu personally devised treatment, and he was blinded in one eye.
translations.idiomatic: At birth he suffered from eye disease; medical treatment always worsened it; Emperor Wu personally devised treatment, and he was blinded in one eye.

sentences.zh: 乃憶先夢，彌加湣愛。

translations.literal: He then recalled the earlier dream and added still more pity and love.
translations.idiomatic: He then recalled the earlier dream and Emperor Wu added still more pity and love.

sentences.zh: 及長好學，博極群書。

translations.literal: When he grew up he loved learning and exhaustively mastered all books.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he loved learning and exhaustively mastered all books.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗問曰：「孫策在江東，于時年幾？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked: "When Sun Ce was in Jiangdong, how old was he?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked, "When Sun Ce was in Jiangdong, how old was he?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「十七。

translations.literal: He answered: "Seventeen."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Seventeen."

sentences.zh: 」武帝曰：「正是汝年。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said: "That is exactly your age."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said, "That is exactly your age."

sentences.zh: 帝性不好聲色，頗慕高名，為荊州刺史，起州學宣尼廟。

translations.literal: By nature he did not love music and women; he greatly admired high reputation; as Inspector of Jingzhou he built a provincial school and a temple to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he cared little for music and women and greatly admired men of reputation; as Inspector of Jingzhou he built a provincial school and a temple to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 嘗置儒林參軍一人，勸學從事二人，生三十人，加廩餼。

translations.literal: He once appointed one Scholar of the Confucian Grove, two Encouragers of Learning, and thirty students, increasing their grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed one Scholar of the Confucian Grove, two Encouragers of Learning, and thirty students, increasing their grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 帝工書善畫，自圖宣尼像，為之贊而書之，時人謂之三絕。

translations.literal: The Emperor was skilled at calligraphy and painting; he himself painted the image of Confucius, composed a eulogy and wrote it, and contemporaries called it a triple masterpiece.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at calligraphy and painting; he himself painted Confucius, composed a eulogy and wrote it, and contemporaries called it a triple masterpiece.

sentences.zh: 與裴子野、劉顯、蕭子雲、張纘及當時才秀為布衣交。

translations.literal: With Pei Ziye, Liu Xian, Xiao Ziyun, Zhang Zuan, and the talented men of the time he formed friendships as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: With Pei Ziye, Liu Xian, Xiao Ziyun, Zhang Zuan, and the talented men of the time he formed friendships as equals.

sentences.zh: 常自比諸葛亮、桓溫，惟纘許焉。

translations.literal: He often compared himself to Zhuge Liang and Huan Wen; only Zhang Zuan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He often compared himself to Zhuge Liang and Huan Wen; only Zhang Zuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 性好矯飾，多猜忌，於名無所假人。

translations.literal: His nature loved affectation and was much given to suspicion; in reputation he yielded nothing to others.
translations.idiomatic: His nature loved affectation and was much given to suspicion; in reputation he yielded nothing to others.

sentences.zh: 微有勝己者，必加毀害。

translations.literal: If someone slightly surpassed him, he was sure to add slander and harm.
translations.idiomatic: If someone slightly surpassed him, he was sure to slander and destroy them.

sentences.zh: 帝姑義興昭長公主子王銓兄弟八九人有盛名。

translations.literal: The Emperor's aunt's son Wang Quan and his eight or nine brothers had great fame.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's aunt's son Wang Quan and his eight or nine brothers had great fame.

sentences.zh: 帝妒害其美，遂改寵姬王氏兄王珩名琳以同其父名。

translations.literal: The Emperor, jealous of their excellence, changed the name of his favored consort's brother Wang Heng to Lin to match her father's name.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, jealous of their excellence, changed the name of his favored consort's brother Wang Heng to Lin to match her father's name.

sentences.zh: 忌劉之遴學，使人鴆之。

translations.literal: He envied Liu Zhi's learning and had someone poison him.
translations.idiomatic: He envied Liu Zhi's learning and had someone poison him.

sentences.zh: 如此者甚眾，雖骨肉亦遍被其禍。

translations.literal: There were very many such cases; even kin by blood were everywhere struck by this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: There were very many such cases; even kin by blood were everywhere struck by this calamity.

sentences.zh: 始居文宣太后憂，依丁蘭作木母。

translations.literal: When he first entered mourning for Empress Dowager Wenxuan, following Ding Lan he made a wooden mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered mourning for Empress Dowager Wenxuan, following Ding Lan he made a wooden mother.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩，秘喪逾年，乃發凶問，方刻檀為像，置於百福殿內，事之甚謹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died he kept the death secret for more than a year before announcing the mourning news; only then did he carve a sandalwood image and place it in Baifu Hall, serving it with utmost reverence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died he kept the death secret for more than a year before announcing the mourning news; only then did he carve a sandalwood image and place it in Baifu Hall, serving it with utmost reverence.

sentences.zh: 朝夕進蔬食，動靜必啟聞，跡其虛矯如此。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he offered vegetarian food; in every movement he reported to it—his hypocrisy was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening he offered vegetarian food; in every movement he reported to it—his hypocrisy was such as this.

sentences.zh: 性愛書籍，既患目，多不自執卷，置讀書左右，番次上直，晝夜為常，略無休已，雖睡，卷猶不釋。

translations.literal: He loved books by nature; since his eyes were afflicted he mostly did not hold scrolls himself but placed readers at his side in rotating shifts day and night as a constant, scarcely resting; even in sleep the scroll was not released.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books by nature; since his eyes were afflicted he mostly did not hold scrolls himself but placed readers at his side in rotating shifts day and night as a constant, scarcely resting; even in sleep the scroll was not released.

sentences.zh: 五人各伺一更，恒致達曉。

translations.literal: Five men each waited one watch and always read until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Five men each waited one watch and always read until dawn.

sentences.zh: 常眠熟大鼾，左右有睡，讀失次第，或偷卷度紙。

translations.literal: When he slept deeply he snored loudly; if those beside him slept, the reading lost its order, or someone secretly turned pages ahead.
translations.idiomatic: When he slept deeply he snored loudly; if those beside him slept, the reading lost its order, or someone secretly turned pages ahead.

sentences.zh: 帝必驚覺，更令追讀，加以檟楚。

translations.literal: The Emperor would surely start awake, order the passage read again, and add beating with the whip.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would surely start awake, order the passage read again, and add beating with the whip.

sentences.zh: 雖戎略殷湊，機務繁多，軍書羽檄，文章詔誥，點毫便就，殆不遊手。

translations.literal: Though military strategy pressed close and routine affairs were numerous, military dispatches, urgent reports, literary compositions, and edicts—all were completed at a stroke of the brush, scarcely leaving his hand idle.
translations.idiomatic: Though military strategy pressed close and routine affairs were numerous, military dispatches, urgent reports, literary compositions, and edicts—all were completed at a stroke of the brush, scarcely leaving his hand idle.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「我韜于文士，愧于武夫。

translations.literal: He often said: "I am concealed among literary men and ashamed before martial men."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "I am concealed among literary men and ashamed before martial men."

sentences.zh: 」論者以為得言。

translations.literal: Commentators thought this well said.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators thought this well said.

sentences.zh: 始在尋陽，夢人曰：「天下將亂，王必維之。

translations.literal: When he was first at Xunyang, a man in a dream said to him: "The realm will fall into disorder—you must hold it together."
translations.idiomatic: When he was first at Xunyang, a man in a dream said to him, "The realm will fall into disorder—you must hold it together."

sentences.zh: 」又背生黑子，巫媼見曰：「此大貴不可言。

translations.literal: Again a black mole grew on his back; an old woman who saw it said: "This is great nobility beyond words."
translations.idiomatic: Again a black mole grew on his back; an old woman who saw it said, "This is great nobility beyond words."

sentences.zh: 」初，武帝敕賀革為帝府諮議，使講三禮。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu ordered He Ge to serve as Adviser to the Prince's establishment and lecture on the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Wu ordered He Ge to serve as Adviser to the Prince's establishment and lecture on the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 革西上，意甚不悅，過別御史中丞江革。

translations.literal: Ge went west and was very displeased; passing by he took leave of the Censor-in-Chief Jiang Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Ge went west and was very displeased; passing by he took leave of Censor-in-Chief Jiang Ge.

sentences.zh: 江革告之曰：「吾嘗夢主上遍見諸子，至湘東王，脫帽授之。

translations.literal: Jiang Ge told him: "I once dreamed the sovereign visited all his sons; when he came to the Prince of Xiangdong he removed his cap and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ge told him, "I once dreamed the sovereign visited all his sons; when he came to the Prince of Xiangdong he removed his cap and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 此人後必當璧，卿其行乎。

translations.literal: This man will later surely receive the jade disk—you should go."
translations.idiomatic: This man will later surely receive the jade disk—you should go."

sentences.zh: 」革頷之。

translations.literal: Ge nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: Ge nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 及太清之禍，遂膺歸運。

translations.literal: When the calamity of Taiqing came, he then received the mandate of return.
translations.idiomatic: When the calamity of Taiqing came, he then received the mandate of return.

sentences.zh: 自侯景之難，州郡太半入魏，自巴陵以下至建康，緣以長江為限。

translations.literal: From the disaster of Hou Jing, more than half the provinces and commanderies entered Wei; from Baling south to Jiankang, the Yangzi River formed the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: From the disaster of Hou Jing, more than half the provinces and commanderies entered Wei; from Baling south to Jiankang, the Yangzi River formed the boundary.

sentences.zh: 荊州界北盡武寧，西拒峽口；

translations.literal: North of Jingzhou the border reached Wuning; west it resisted the gorge mouth;
translations.idiomatic: North of Jingzhou the border reached Wuning; west it reached the gorge mouth;

sentences.zh: 自嶺以南，復為蕭勃所據。

translations.literal: south of the ranges it was again held by Xiao Bo.
translations.idiomatic: south of the ranges it was again held by Xiao Bo.

sentences.zh: 文軌所同，千里而近，人戶著籍，不盈三萬。

translations.literal: Where the written tradition was unified was nearly a thousand li; registered households did not exceed thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Where the written tradition was unified was nearly a thousand li; registered households did not exceed thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 中興之盛，盡於是矣。

translations.literal: The glory of restoration ended here.
translations.idiomatic: The glory of restoration ended here.

sentences.zh: 武陵之平，議者欲因其舟艦遷都建鄴，宗懍、黃羅漢皆楚人，不願移，帝及胡僧佑亦俱未欲動。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Wuling, deliberators wished to move the capital to Jiankang using their boats; Zong Lin and Huang Luohan were both men of Chu and did not wish to move; the Emperor and Hu Sengyou also both did not wish to stir.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Wuling, deliberators wished to move the capital to Jiankang using their boats; Zong Lin and Huang Luohan were both men of Chu and did not wish to move; the Emperor and Hu Sengyou also both did not wish to stir.

sentences.zh: 僕射王褒、左戶尚書周弘正驟言即楚非便。

translations.literal: Vice Director Wang Bao and the Director of the Left Household Ministry Zhou Hongzheng repeatedly said that immediate removal to Chu was not advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Bao and Director of the Left Household Ministry Zhou Hongzheng repeatedly said that immediate removal to Chu was not advantageous.

sentences.zh: 宗懍及御史中丞劉懿以為建鄴王氣已盡，且渚宮洲已滿百，於是乃留。

translations.literal: Zong Lin and the Censor-in-Chief Liu Yi thought the royal qi of Jiankang was already exhausted, and moreover the islet of Zhugong Palace was already full to a hundred—therefore they remained.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Lin and Censor-in-Chief Liu Yi thought the royal qi of Jiankang was already exhausted, and moreover the islet of Zhugong Palace was already full to a hundred—therefore they remained.

sentences.zh: 尋而歲星在井，熒惑守心，帝觀之慨然而謂朝臣文武曰：「吾觀玄象，將恐有賊。

translations.literal: Soon the year star was in the Well; Mars guarded the Heart; the Emperor observed them and said sighing to the civil and military court: "I observe the celestial signs—I fear there will be rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the year star was in the Well; Mars guarded the Heart; the Emperor observed them and said sighing to the civil and military court, "I observe the celestial signs—I fear there will be rebels.

sentences.zh: 但吉凶在我，運數由天，避之何益？

translations.literal: But fortune and calamity depend on me; fate is ordained by Heaven—what good is avoidance?"
translations.idiomatic: But fortune and calamity depend on me; fate is ordained by Heaven—what good is avoidance?"

sentences.zh: 」及魏軍逼，閽人朱買臣按劍進曰：「惟有斬宗懍、黃羅漢，可以謝天下。

translations.literal: When Wei troops pressed close, the gatekeeper Zhu Maichen drew his sword and advanced, saying: "Only by executing Zong Lin and Huang Luohan can the realm be appeased."
translations.idiomatic: When Wei troops pressed close, gatekeeper Zhu Maichen drew his sword and advanced, saying, "Only by executing Zong Lin and Huang Luohan can the realm be appeased."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「曩實吾意，宗、黃何罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "It was indeed my intention—what crime have Zong and Huang?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "It was indeed my intention—what crime have Zong and Huang?"

sentences.zh: 」二人退入于人中。

translations.literal: The two withdrew into the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: The two withdrew into the crowd.

sentences.zh: 及魏人燒柵，買臣、謝答仁勸帝乘暗潰圍出就任約。

translations.literal: When Wei men burned the palisades, Maichen and Xie Daren urged the Emperor to slip out under cover of darkness and go to Ren Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei men burned the palisades, Maichen and Xie Daren urged the Emperor to slip out under cover of darkness and go to Ren Yue.

sentences.zh: 帝素不便馳馬，曰：「事必無成，徒增辱耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor had never been skilled at riding and said: "The affair will surely not succeed—it will only add disgrace."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had never been skilled at riding and said, "The affair will surely not succeed—it will only add disgrace."

sentences.zh: 」答仁又求自扶，帝以問僕射王褒。

translations.literal: Daren again asked to support him himself; the Emperor asked Vice Director Wang Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Daren again asked to support him himself; the Emperor asked Vice Director Wang Bao.

sentences.zh: 褒曰：「答仁，侯景之黨，豈是可信？

translations.literal: Bao said: "Daren is a partisan of Hou Jing—how can he be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: Bao said, "Daren is a partisan of Hou Jing—how can he be trusted?

sentences.zh: 成彼之勳，不如降也。

translations.literal: To achieve his merit, it would be better to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: To achieve his merit, it would be better to surrender."

sentences.zh: 」乃聚圖書十餘萬卷盡燒之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered more than a hundred thousand scrolls of books and burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they gathered more than a hundred thousand scrolls of books and burned them all.

sentences.zh: 答仁又請守子城，收兵可得五千人。

translations.literal: Daren again asked to hold the inner city and gather troops—five thousand could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Daren again asked to hold the inner city and gather troops—five thousand could be obtained.

sentences.zh: 帝然之，即授城內大都督，以帝鼓吹給之，配以公主。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved and immediately appointed him Grand Commander of the Inner City, gave him the imperial music, and paired him with a princess.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and immediately appointed him Grand Commander of the Inner City, gave him the imperial music, and paired him with a princess.

sentences.zh: 既而又召王褒謀之，答仁請入不得，歐血而去。

translations.literal: Soon he again summoned Wang Bao to deliberate; Daren asked to enter but could not and spat blood and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again summoned Wang Bao to deliberate; Daren asked to enter but could not and spat blood and departed.

sentences.zh: 遂使皇太子、王褒出質請降。

translations.literal: He then sent the Crown Prince and Wang Bao out as hostages to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent the Crown Prince and Wang Bao out as hostages to request surrender.

sentences.zh: 有頃，黃門郎裴政犯門而出。

translations.literal: Before long the Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pei Zheng broke through the gate and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pei Zheng broke through the gate and went out.

sentences.zh: 帝乘白馬素衣出東門，抽劍擊闔曰：「蕭世誠一至此乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor rode a white horse in plain clothes out the eastern gate, drew his sword and struck the gate bar, saying: "Has Xiao Shicheng come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rode a white horse in plain clothes out the eastern gate, drew his sword and struck the gate bar, saying, "Has Xiao Shicheng come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」魏師至凡二十八日，徵兵四方，未至而城見克。

translations.literal: Wei troops were at the city for twenty-eight days in all; troops were summoned from the four quarters but did not arrive before the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops were at the city for twenty-eight days in all; troops were summoned from the four quarters but did not arrive before the city fell.

sentences.zh: 在幽逼，求酒飲之，制詩四絕。

translations.literal: Under confinement he asked for wine and drank it, and composed four quatrains.
translations.idiomatic: Under confinement he asked for wine and drank it, and composed four quatrains.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：「南風且絕唱，西陵最可悲，今日還蒿裏，終非封禪時。

translations.literal: The first reads: "The southern wind now ends its song; Xiling is most pitiable—today I return to the wild grave; this is not the time for the feng and shan rites."
translations.idiomatic: The first reads: "The southern wind now ends its song; Xiling is most pitiable—today I return to the wild grave; this is not the time for the feng and shan rites."

sentences.zh: 」其二曰：「人世逢百六，天道異貞恒，何言異螻蟻，一旦損從鵬。

translations.literal: The second reads: "The human world meets the hundred-six; the Way of Heaven differs from constancy—why speak of differing from ants; in one morning the follower-peng is lost."
translations.idiomatic: The second reads: "The human world meets the hundred-six; the Way of Heaven differs from constancy—why speak of differing from ants; in one morning the follower-peng is lost."

sentences.zh: 」其三曰：「松風侵曉哀，霜雰當夜來，寂寥千載後，誰畏軒轅台。

translations.literal: The third reads: "Pine wind invades the dawn with grief; frost clouds come in the night; lonely after a thousand years—who fears the Terrace of Xuanyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: The third reads: "Pine wind invades the dawn with grief; frost clouds come in the night; lonely after a thousand years—who fears the Terrace of Xuanyuan?"

sentences.zh: 」其四曰：「夜長無歲月，安知秋與春？

translations.literal: The fourth reads: "The night is long without months and years—how know autumn from spring?
translations.idiomatic: The fourth reads: "The night is long without months and years—how know autumn from spring?

sentences.zh: 原陵五樹杏，空得動耕人。

translations.literal: At Yuan Mausoleum five apricot trees—only able to move the plowman."
translations.idiomatic: At Yuan Mausoleum five apricot trees—only able to move the plowman."

sentences.zh: 」梁王察遣尚書傅准監行刑，帝謂之曰：「卿幸為我宣行。

translations.literal: The King of Liang Cha sent the Director of the Masters of Writing Fu Zhun to supervise the execution; the Emperor said to him: "I rely on you to proclaim the deed."
translations.idiomatic: King of Liang Cha sent Director of the Masters of Writing Fu Zhun to supervise the execution; the Emperor said to him, "I rely on you to proclaim the deed."

sentences.zh: 」准捧詩，流淚不能禁，進土囊而殞之。

translations.literal: Zhun held the poems, wept and could not restrain himself, advanced a bag of earth, and the Emperor perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun held the poems, wept and could not restrain himself, advanced a bag of earth, and the Emperor perished.

sentences.zh: 梁王察使以布帊纏屍，斂以蒲席，束以白茅，以車一乘，葬于津陽門外。

translations.literal: The King of Liang Cha had the corpse wrapped in cloth, collected in rush matting, bound with white thatch, and buried with one carriage outside Jinyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: King of Liang Cha had the corpse wrapped in cloth, collected in rush matting, bound with white thatch, and buried with one carriage outside Jinyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子元良及始安王方略等，皆見害。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai Yuanliang and the Prince of Shi'an Fanglue and others were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai Yuanliang and Prince Fanglue of Shi'an and others were all killed.

sentences.zh: 徐世譜、任約自馬頭走巴陵。

translations.literal: Xu Shipu and Ren Yue fled from Matou to Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shipu and Ren Yue fled from Matou to Baling.

sentences.zh: 約後降于齊。

translations.literal: Yue later surrendered to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue later surrendered to Qi.

sentences.zh: 將軍裴畿、畿弟機並被害。

translations.literal: The generals Pei Ji and Ji's younger brother Ji were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Pei Ji and Ji's younger brother Ji were both killed.

sentences.zh: 謝答仁三人相抱，俱見屠。

translations.literal: Xie Daren and three others embraced one another and were all slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Daren and three others embraced one another and were all slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 汝南王大封、尚書左僕射王褒以下，並為俘以歸長安。

translations.literal: The Prince of Runan Dafeng, Left Vice Director Wang Bao, and those below were all taken captive and sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Da-feng of Runan, Left Vice Director Wang Bao, and those below were all taken captive and sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 乃選百姓男女數萬口，分為奴婢，小弱者皆殺之。

translations.literal: They then selected tens of thousands of men and women among the common people, divided them as slaves and maidservants, and killed the small and weak.
translations.idiomatic: They then selected tens of thousands of men and women among the common people, divided them as slaves and maidservants, and killed the small and weak.

sentences.zh: 帝於伎術無所不該，嘗不得南信，筮之，遇剝之艮。

translations.literal: The Emperor was versed in every craft of skill; once when he could not obtain news from the south he divined and encountered Gen of Stripping.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was versed in every craft of skill; once when he could not obtain news from the south he divined and encountered Gen of Stripping.

sentences.zh: 曰：「南信已至，今當遣左右季心往看」。

translations.literal: He said: "Southern news has already arrived—now I shall send the attendant Ji Xin to look."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Southern news has already arrived—now I shall send the attendant Ji Xin to look."

sentences.zh: 果如所說，賓客咸驚其妙。

translations.literal: It was indeed as he said, and guests were all startled at his subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: It was indeed as he said, and guests were all startled at his subtlety.

sentences.zh: 凡所占決皆然。

translations.literal: Every divination and decision was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Every divination and decision was thus.

sentences.zh: 初從劉景受相術，因訊以年，答曰：「未至五十，當有小厄，禳之可免。

translations.literal: At first he received physiognomy from Liu Jing and asked his age; he answered: "Before reaching fifty there will be a small calamity—if suppressed it can be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: At first he received physiognomy from Liu Jing and asked his age; he answered, "Before reaching fifty there will be a small calamity—if suppressed it can be avoided."

sentences.zh: 」帝自勉曰：「苟有期會，禳之何益？

translations.literal: The Emperor encouraged himself: "If there is a fixed term, what good is suppression?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor encouraged himself, "If there is a fixed term, what good is suppression?"

sentences.zh: 」灨敘四十七矣。

translations.literal: He was forty-seven at the time of the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-seven at the time of the disaster.

sentences.zh: 特多禁忌，牆壁崩倒，屋宇傾頹，年月不便，終不修改。

translations.literal: He had many taboos; when walls collapsed or buildings tilted, if the year and month were inauspicious he would never repair them.
translations.idiomatic: He had many taboos; when walls collapsed or buildings tilted, if the year and month were inauspicious he would never repair them.

sentences.zh: 庭草蕪沒，令鞭去之，其慎護如此。

translations.literal: Courtyard grass overgrew and he ordered it whipped away—his careful protection was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Courtyard grass overgrew and he ordered it whipped away—his careful protection was such as this.

sentences.zh: 著孝德傳、忠臣傳各三十卷，丹陽尹傳十卷，注漢書一百十五卷，周易講疏十卷，內典博要百卷，連山三十卷、詞林三卷，玉韜、金樓子、補闕子各十卷，老子講疏四卷，懷舊傳二卷，古今全德志、荊南地記、貢職圖、古今同姓名錄一卷，筮經十二卷，式贊三卷，文集五十卷。

translations.literal: His works included Biographies of Filial Virtue and Biographies of Loyal Ministers each in thirty juan, Biographies of the Directors of Danyang in ten juan, a Commentary on the Book of Han in one hundred fifteen juan, Exegesis of the Book of Changes in ten juan, Essentials of the Inner Canon in one hundred juan, Lianshan in thirty juan and Forest of Phrases in three juan, Jade Sheath, Lord of the Golden Tower, and Supplement to the Deficient each in ten juan, Exegesis of Laozi in four juan, Record of Reminiscence in two juan, Record of Complete Virtues Ancient and Modern, Geography of Jingnan, Tribute Diagram, and Record of Identical Names Ancient and Modern each in one juan, Classic of Divination in twelve juan, Praise of the Mold in three juan, and Collected Works in fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Biographies of Filial Virtue and Biographies of Loyal Ministers each in thirty juan, Biographies of the Directors of Danyang in ten juan, a Commentary on the Book of Han in one hundred fifteen juan, Exegesis of the Book of Changes in ten juan, Essentials of the Inner Canon in one hundred juan, Lianshan in thirty juan and Forest of Phrases in three juan, Jade Sheath, Lord of the Golden Tower, and Supplement to the Deficient each in ten juan, Exegesis of Laozi in four juan, Record of Reminiscence in two juan, Record of Complete Virtues Ancient and Modern, Geography of Jingnan, Tribute Diagram, and Record of Identical Names Ancient and Modern each in one juan, Classic of Divination in twelve juan, Praise of the Mold in three juan, and Collected Works in fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 敬皇帝諱方智，字慧相，小字法真，元帝第九子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing was named Fangzhi, courtesy name Huixiang, childhood name Fazhen; he was the ninth son of Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing was named Fangzhi, courtesy name Huixiang, childhood name Fazhen, and was the ninth son of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，封興梁侯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingliang.

sentences.zh: 四年二月癸丑，于江州奉迎至建鄴，入居朝堂。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, second month, on guichou, he was received from Jiangzhou to Jiankang and entered the Court Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, second month, on guichou, he was received from Jiangzhou to Jiankang and entered the Court Hall.

sentences.zh: 以太尉王僧辯為中書監、錄尚書、驃騎大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，加司空陳霸先班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Sengbian was appointed Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, General of Agile Cavalry, and Commander-in-Chief of Inner and Outer Forces; Minister of Works Chen Baxian was granted twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Sengbian was appointed Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, General of Agile Cavalry, and Commander-in-Chief of Inner and Outer Forces; Minister of Works Chen Baxian was granted twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 以湘州刺史蕭循為太尉，廣州刺史蕭勃為司徒。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou Inspector Xiao Xun was appointed Grand Commandant; Guangzhou Inspector Xiao Bo was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou Inspector Xiao Xun was made Grand Commandant; Guangzhou Inspector Xiao Bo was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三月，齊遣其上党王高渙送貞陽侯蕭明來主梁嗣，至東關，遣吳興太守裴之橫拒之。

translations.literal: In the third month Qi sent the Prince of Shangdang Gao Huan to escort the Marquis of Zhenyang Xiao Ming to take the Liang succession; reaching Dongguan, he sent Wuxing Administrator Pei Zhiheng to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Qi sent Prince Gao Huan of Shangdang to escort Marquis Xiao Ming of Zhenyang to take the Liang succession; reaching Dongguan, he sent Wuxing Administrator Pei Zhiheng to resist him.

sentences.zh: 與戰，敗績，死之。

translations.literal: They fought; he was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: They fought; he was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 四月，司徒陸法和以郢州附齊，遣江州刺史侯瑱討之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Minister of Works Lu Fahé submitted Yingzhou to Qi; Jiangzhou Inspector Hou Tian was ordered to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Minister of Works Lu Fahé submitted Yingzhou to Qi; Jiangzhou Inspector Hou Tian was ordered to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 七月辛丑，僧辯納貞陽侯蕭明，自採石濟江。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on xinchou, Sengbian received the Marquis of Zhenyang Xiao Ming and crossed the Yangzi from Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on xinchou, Sengbian received Marquis Xiao Ming of Zhenyang and crossed the Yangzi from Caishi.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，入建鄴。

translations.literal: On jiachen he entered Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen he entered Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 丙午，即偽位。

translations.literal: On bingwu he assumed the false throne.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he assumed the false throne.

sentences.zh: 年號天成，以帝為皇太子。

translations.literal: The era name was Tiancheng; the Emperor was made Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was Tiancheng; the Emperor was made Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 司空陳霸先襲殺王僧辯，黜蕭明而奉帝焉。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chen Baxian launched a surprise attack and killed Wang Sengbian, deposed Xiao Ming, and enthroned the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Baxian launched a surprise attack and killed Wang Sengbian, deposed Xiao Ming, and enthroned the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚辰，齊安州刺史翟子崇、楚州刺史劉仕榮、淮州刺史柳達摩率眾赴任約，入石頭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengchen, Qi Inspector of Anzhou Zhai Zichong, Inspector of Chuzhou Liu Shirong, and Inspector of Huaizhou Liu Damo led troops to join Ren Yue and entered Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengchen, Qi Inspector of Anzhou Zhai Zichong, Inspector of Chuzhou Liu Shirong, and Inspector of Huaizhou Liu Damo led troops to join Ren Yue and entered Shitou.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚戌，任約、徐嗣徽等至採石迎齊援。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengxu, Ren Yue, Xu Sihui, and others reached Caishi to welcome Qi reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengxu, Ren Yue, Xu Sihui, and others reached Caishi to welcome Qi reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，遣猛烈將軍侯安都于江寧邀擊，敗之，約、嗣徽等奔江西。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Fierce General Hou Andu intercepted and attacked them at Jiangning; he defeated them, and Yue, Sihui, and others fled west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Fierce General Hou Andu intercepted and attacked them at Jiangning; he defeated them, and Yue, Sihui, and others fled west of the river.

sentences.zh: 庚申，翟子崇等降，並放還北。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Zhai Zichong and the others surrendered and were all sent back north.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Zhai Zichong and the others surrendered and were all sent back north.

sentences.zh: 太平元年春正月戊寅，大赦。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Taiping, on wuyin, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the first year of Taiping, on wuyin, a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 追贈諡簡文帝諸子。

translations.literal: Posthumous titles were conferred on the sons of Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous titles were conferred on the sons of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 封故永安侯確子後為邵陵王，奉攜王后。

translations.literal: The descendant of the former Marquis of Yong'an Que was enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling to continue the line of Prince Xie.
translations.idiomatic: The descendant of former Marquis Que of Yong'an was enfeoffed as Prince of Shaoling to continue the line of Prince Xie.

sentences.zh: 癸未，震州刺史杜龕降，詔賜死，赦吳興郡。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Zhenzhou Inspector Du Long submitted and was ordered to die by edict; Wu Commandery was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Zhenzhou Inspector Du Long submitted and was ordered to die by edict; Wu Commandery was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 己亥，乙太保宜豐侯蕭循襲封鄱陽王。

translations.literal: On jihai, the late Grand Mentor Marquis Yifeng of Yifeng Xiao Xun inherited the enfeoffment as Prince of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the late Grand Mentor Marquis Yifeng of Yifeng Xiao Xun inherited the enfeoffment as Prince of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 東揚州刺史張彪圍臨海太守王懷振於剡岩。

translations.literal: Eastern Yangzhou Inspector Zhang Biao besieged Linhai Administrator Wang Huaizhen at Shanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yangzhou Inspector Zhang Biao besieged Linhai Administrator Wang Huaizhen at Shanyan.

sentences.zh: 二月庚戌，遣周文育、陳蒨襲會稽討彪，彪敗走。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengxu, Zhou Wenyü and Chen Qian were dispatched to raid Kuaiji and campaign against Biao; Biao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengxu, Zhou Wenyü and Chen Qian were dispatched to raid Kuaiji and campaign against Biao; Biao was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 以中衛將軍臨川王大款即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: General of the Central Guard Prince Dakuan of Linchuan was appointed Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry at his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Central Guard Prince Da-kuan of Linchuan was appointed Commissioner with Grand Cavalry at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，若邪村人斬張彪，傳首建鄴，赦東揚州。

translations.literal: On bingchen, a man of Ruoye Village beheaded Zhang Biao and sent his head to Jiankang; Eastern Yangzhou was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen a man of Ruoye Village beheaded Zhang Biao and sent his head to Jiankang; Eastern Yangzhou was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以東土經杜龕、張彪之亂，遣大使巡省。

translations.literal: On jiazi, because the eastern lands had suffered the disorders of Du Long and Zhang Biao, grand envoys were dispatched to tour and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, because the eastern lands had suffered the disorders of Du Long and Zhang Biao, grand envoys were dispatched to tour and inspect.

sentences.zh: 是月，齊人來聘，使侍中王廓報聘。

translations.literal: That month Qi sent envoys; Attendant Wang Kuo was sent to return the visit.
translations.idiomatic: That month Qi sent envoys; Attendant Wang Kuo was sent to return the visit.

sentences.zh: 三月壬午，班下遠近，並雜用今古錢。

translations.literal: In the third month, on renwu, an edict was issued to the far and near to use both current and ancient coinage mixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renwu, an edict was issued to the far and near to use both current and ancient coinage mixed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，齊將蕭軌出柵口，向梁山，陳霸先大敗之。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Qi general Xiao Gui left Zankou and advanced toward Liangshan; Chen Baxian defeated him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Qi general Xiao Gui left Zankou and advanced toward Liangshan; Chen Baxian defeated him greatly.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬申，侯安都輕兵襲齊行台司馬恭于曆陽，大破之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on renshen, Hou Andu with light troops raided Qi field officer Sima Gong at Liyang and defeated him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on renshen, Hou Andu with light troops raided Qi field officer Sima Gong at Liyang and defeated him greatly.

sentences.zh: 六月壬子，齊軍至玄武湖西北。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renzi, Qi troops reached the northwest of Xuanwu Lake.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi, Qi troops reached the northwest of Xuanwu Lake.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，陳霸先大破齊軍。

translations.literal: On yimao, Chen Baxian defeated the Qi army greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Chen Baxian defeated the Qi army greatly.

sentences.zh: 戊午，大赦。

translations.literal: On wuwu, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，解嚴。

translations.literal: On xinyou, martial law was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou martial law was lifted.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙子，司空陳霸先進位司徒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on bingzi, Minister of Works Chen Baxian was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on bingzi, Minister of Works Chen Baxian was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以開府儀同三司侯瑱為司空。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry Hou Tian was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Commissioner with Grand Cavalry Hou Tian was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八月己酉，太保鄱陽王循薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiyou, Grand Mentor Prince Xun of Poyang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiyou, Grand Mentor Prince Xun of Poyang died.

sentences.zh: 九月壬寅，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renyin, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renyin, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 司徒陳霸先進位丞相、錄尚書事，改封義興郡公。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chen Baxian was promoted to Chancellor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chen Baxian was promoted to Chancellor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 加中權將軍王衝開府儀同三司，以吏部尚書王通為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: General of Central Authority Wang Chong was granted Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry; Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Tong was appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: General of Central Authority Wang Chong was granted Commissioner with Grand Cavalry; Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Tong was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙亥，魏相安定公薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on yihai, the Wei Chancellor the Duke of Anding died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on yihai, Wei Chancellor the Duke of Anding died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，起雲龍、神武門。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Cloud Dragon and Divine Martial gates were built.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Cloud Dragon and Divine Martial gates were built.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬申，進太尉蕭勃為太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renshen, Grand Commandant Xiao Bo was promoted to Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen, Grand Commandant Xiao Bo was promoted to Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 甲午，封前壽昌令劉叡為汝陰王，前鎮西法曹行參軍蕭沇為巴陵王，奉宋、齊二代後。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the former Magistrate of Shouchang Liu Rui was enfeoffed as Prince of Runan, and the former Acting Administrator of the Law Bureau of the Pacifying West Headquarters Xiao Yan was enfeoffed as Prince of Baling, to continue the lines of Song and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu former Magistrate of Shouchang Liu Rui was enfeoffed as Prince of Runan, and former Acting Administrator of the Law Bureau of the Pacifying West Headquarters Xiao Yan was enfeoffed as Prince of Baling, to continue the lines of Song and Qi.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏恭帝遜位於周。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the deposed Emperor of Wei abdicated to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the deposed Emperor of Wei abdicated to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月壬寅，詔求魯國孔氏族為奉聖侯，並繕廟堂，供備祀典。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month, on renyin, an edict sought a member of the Kong clan of Lu as Marquis Who Venerates the Sage, and temple halls were repaired and sacrificial rites supplied.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month, on renyin, an edict sought a member of the Kong clan of Lu as Marquis Who Venerates the Sage, and temple halls were repaired and sacrificial rites supplied.

sentences.zh: 又詔諸州各置中正。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered each province to establish Rectifiers of Central Selection.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered each province to establish Rectifiers of Central Selection.

sentences.zh: 舊放舉選，不得輒承單狀序官，皆須中正押上，然後量授。

translations.literal: Formerly in nominations for office one could not directly submit a single petition for appointment—all required the Rectifier's endorsement before rank was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in nominations for office one could not directly submit a single petition for appointment—all required the Rectifier's endorsement before rank was granted.

sentences.zh: 其選中正，每求耆德該悉，以他官領之。

translations.literal: In selecting Rectifiers, each time venerable virtue and comprehensive knowledge were sought, and another official held the post concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting Rectifiers, each time venerable virtue and comprehensive knowledge were sought, and another official held the post concurrently.

sentences.zh: 以開府儀同三司王琳為司空，以尚書右僕射王通為左僕射。

translations.literal: Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry Wang Lin was appointed Minister of Works; Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Tong was appointed Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner with Grand Cavalry Wang Lin was made Minister of Works; Right Vice Director Wang Tong was made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 二月庚午，遣領軍將軍徐度入東關。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengwu, General of the Palace Guard Xu Du entered Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu, General of the Palace Guard Xu Du entered Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 太保、廣州刺史蕭勃舉兵反，詔平西將軍周文育、平南將軍侯安都等南討。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor and Guangzhou Inspector Xiao Bo raised troops in rebellion; General Who Pacifies the West Zhou Wenyü and General Who Pacifies the South Hou Andu and others were ordered to campaign south.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor and Guangzhou Inspector Xiao Bo raised troops in rebellion; General Who Pacifies the West Zhou Wenyü and General Who Pacifies the South Hou Andu and others were ordered to campaign south.

sentences.zh: 戊子，徐度至合肥，燒齊船舶三千艘。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Xu Du reached Hefei and burned three thousand Qi ships.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Xu Du reached Hefei and burned three thousand Qi ships.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，周文育軍于巴山，獲蕭勃偽帥歐陽頠。

translations.literal: On guisi, Zhou Wenyü's army was at Bashan and captured Xiao Bo's false commander Ouyang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Zhou Wenyü's army was at Bashan and captured Xiao Bo's false commander Ouyang Yi.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅，德州刺史陳法武、前衡州刺史譚遠于始興攻殺蕭勃。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, Dezhou Inspector Chen Fawu and former Hengzhou Inspector Tan Yuan attacked and killed Xiao Bo at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin, Dezhou Inspector Chen Fawu and former Hengzhou Inspector Tan Yuan attacked and killed Xiao Bo at Shixing.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸酉，曲赦江、廣、衡三州，並督內為賊所拘逼者。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on guiyou, a partial amnesty was granted to Jiang, Guang, and Heng provinces and all within their jurisdictions who had been coerced by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on guiyou, a partial amnesty was granted to Jiang, Guang, and Heng provinces and all within their jurisdictions who had been coerced by rebels.

sentences.zh: 己卯，鑄四柱錢，一當二十。

translations.literal: On jimao, four-pillar coin was cast, one equal to twenty.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao four-pillar coin was cast, one equal to twenty.

sentences.zh: 齊遣使通和。

translations.literal: Qi sent envoys seeking peace.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent envoys seeking peace.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，改四柱錢，一當十。

translations.literal: On renchen, the four-pillar coin was changed—one equal to ten.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the four-pillar coin was changed—one equal to ten.

sentences.zh: 丙申，復閉細錢。

translations.literal: On bingshen, small coin was again closed from circulation.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen small coin was again closed from circulation.

sentences.zh: 五月乙巳，平西將軍周文育進號鎮南將軍，平南將軍侯安都進號鎮北將軍，並開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi, General Who Pacifies the West Zhou Wenyü was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South; General Who Pacifies the South Hou Andu was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North—both were granted Commissioner with the Grand Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yisi, General Who Pacifies the West Zhou Wenyü was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South; General Who Pacifies the South Hou Andu was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North—both were granted Commissioner with Grand Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，余孝頃遣使詣丞相府求降。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Yu Xiaoxiang sent envoys to the Chancellor's office seeking surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Yu Xiaoxiang sent envoys to the Chancellor's office seeking surrender.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，加丞相陳霸先殊禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, extraordinary honors were added to Chancellor Chen Baxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn extraordinary honors were added to Chancellor Chen Baxian.

sentences.zh: 九月，周塚宰宇文護殺閔帝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zhou Regent Yuwen Hu killed Emperor Min.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhou Regent Yuwen Hu killed Emperor Min.

sentences.zh: 丞相陳霸先改授相國，封陳國公。

translations.literal: Chancellor Chen Baxian was reappointed Chancellor and enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chen Baxian was reappointed Chancellor and enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 論曰：帝王之位，天下之重職，文武之道，守國所常遵。

translations.literal: Commentary says: The position of emperor and king is the weightiest duty under Heaven; the Way of wen and wu is what guarding the state constantly follows.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary says: The position of emperor and king is the weightiest duty under Heaven; the Way of wen and wu is what guarding the state constantly follows.

sentences.zh: 其於行用，義均水火，相資則可，專任成亂。

translations.literal: In their employment, righteousness is like water and fire—mutual support is possible, exclusive reliance brings disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In their employment, righteousness is like water and fire—mutual support is possible, exclusive reliance brings disorder.

sentences.zh: 觀夫有梁諸帝，皆一之而已。

translations.literal: Observing the emperors of Liang, each had only one of the two.
translations.idiomatic: Observing the emperors of Liang, each had only one of the two.

sentences.zh: 簡文文明之姿，稟乎天授，粵自支庶，入居明兩，經國之算，其道弗聞。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen's civil brilliance was endowed by Heaven; from a branch line he entered the bright position; the strategy of governing the state—its Way was not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen's civil brilliance was endowed by Heaven; from a branch line he entered the bright position; the strategy of governing the state—its Way was not heard.

sentences.zh: 宮體所傳，且變朝野，雖主虛號，何救滅亡。

translations.literal: What the Palace Style transmitted changed court and countryside; though he held an empty title, what could save extinction?
translations.idiomatic: What the Palace Style transmitted changed court and countryside; though he held an empty title, what could save extinction?

sentences.zh: 元帝居勢勝之地，啟中興之業，既雪讎恥，且應天人。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan occupied a position of superior strength and opened the enterprise of restoration; he both wiped away grievance and shame and answered Heaven and men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan occupied a position of superior strength and opened the enterprise of restoration; he both wiped away grievance and shame and answered Heaven and men.

sentences.zh: 而內積猜忍，外崇矯飾，攀號之節，忍酷於踰年；

translations.literal: Yet inwardly he accumulated suspicion and cruelty; outwardly he exalted affectation; in the rites of proclaiming the mourning name he was cruel beyond a year;
translations.idiomatic: Yet inwardly he accumulated suspicion and cruelty; outwardly he exalted affectation; in the rites of proclaiming the mourning name he was cruel beyond a year;

sentences.zh: 定省之制，申情於木偶。

translations.literal: in the regulations of visiting parents he expressed feeling toward a wooden image.
translations.idiomatic: in the regulations of visiting parents he expressed feeling toward a wooden image.

sentences.zh: 竟而雍州引寇，釁起河東之戮，益部親尋，事習邵陵之窘。

translations.literal: In the end Yongzhou drew in invaders; the provocation began with the slaughter at Hedong; Yizhou turned kin against kin; the affair followed the distress of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Yongzhou drew in invaders; the provocation began with the slaughter at Hedong; Yizhou turned kin against kin; the affair followed the distress of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 悖辭屈於僧辯，殘虐極於圓正，不義不昵，若斯之甚。

translations.literal: Perverse words bowed before Sengbian; cruelty reached its limit at Yuanzheng; unrighteous and unkind—to such a degree.
translations.idiomatic: Perverse words bowed before Sengbian; cruelty reached its limit at Yuanzheng; unrighteous and unkind—to such a degree.

sentences.zh: 而復謀無經遠，心勞志大，近舍宗國，遠迫強鄰，外弛藩籬，內崇講肆，卒於溘至戕隕，方追始皇之跡，雖復文籍滿腹，何救社廟之墟。

translations.literal: Yet again his plans lacked far sight; his heart toiled and his ambition was great; near at hand he abandoned the ancestral state, far off he pressed a strong neighbor; outwardly he relaxed the frontier defenses, inwardly he exalted lecture halls—and he ended in sudden slaughter and fall, treading in the tracks of the First Emperor; though books filled his belly, what could save the ruins of the altars?
translations.idiomatic: Yet again his plans lacked far sight; his heart toiled and his ambition was great; near at hand he abandoned the ancestral state, far off he pressed a strong neighbor; outwardly he relaxed the frontier defenses, inwardly he exalted lecture halls—and he ended in sudden slaughter and fall, treading in the tracks of the First Emperor; though books filled his belly, what could save the ruins of the altars?

sentences.zh: 曆觀書契以來，蓋亦廢興代有，未見三葉遘湣，頓若蕭宗之酷。

translations.literal: Reviewing written records from antiquity, rise and fall have always alternated—but never seen were three generations meeting calamity as sudden and cruel as the house of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing written records from antiquity, rise and fall have always alternated—but never seen were three generations meeting calamity as sudden and cruel as the house of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 敬皇以此沖年，當斯頹運，將不高揖，其可得乎。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing at such a tender age faced this declining fortune—if he did not yield the throne high, how could it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing at such a tender age faced this declining fortune—if he did not yield the throne high, how could it be obtained?

sentences.zh: 初，武帝末年，都下用錢，每百皆除其九，謂為九佰，竟而有侯景之亂。

translations.literal: At first, in the late years of Emperor Wu, coin used in the capital had nine of every hundred removed, called the "nine hundred"—and in the end came the disorder of Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the late years of Emperor Wu, coin used in the capital had nine of every hundred removed, called the "nine hundred"—and in the end came the disorder of Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 及江陵將覆，每百復除六文，稱為六佰。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was about to fall, again six cash of every hundred were removed, called the "six hundred."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was about to fall, again six cash of every hundred were removed, called the "six hundred."

sentences.zh: 識者以為九者陽九，六者百六，蓋符歷數，非人事也。

translations.literal: Those who understood thought nine was the yang nine and six was the hundred-six—surely symbols of the calendar's numbers, not human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood thought nine was the yang nine and six was the hundred-six—surely symbols of the calendar's numbers, not human affairs.

sentences.zh: 善乎鄭文貞公論之曰：高祖固天攸縱，聰明稽古，道亞生知，學為博物，允文允武，多藝多才。

translations.literal: Excellent is the commentary of Duke Zhen of Zheng, who said: The High Ancestor was indeed Heaven's chosen, intelligent and versed in antiquity; his Way nearly matched innate knowledge, his learning was that of broad learning; he was both wen and wu, with many arts and many talents.
translations.idiomatic: Excellent is the commentary of Duke Zhen of Zheng, who said: The High Ancestor was indeed Heaven's chosen, intelligent and versed in antiquity; his Way nearly matched innate knowledge, his learning was that of broad learning; he was both wen and wu, with many arts and many talents.

sentences.zh: 爰自諸生，有不羈之度，屬昏凶肆虐，天倫及禍，糾合義旅，將雪家冤。

translations.literal: From his days as a student he had an untamed spirit; when the wicked and fierce ran rampant and family bonds met calamity, he gathered righteous troops to wipe away the family's wrong.
translations.idiomatic: From his days as a student he had an untamed spirit; when the wicked and fierce ran rampant and family bonds met calamity, he gathered righteous troops to wipe away the family's wrong.

sentences.zh: 曰紂可伐，不期而會，龍躍樊、漢，電擊湘、郢。

translations.literal: He said Zhou could be punished; without expecting it they assembled; he leapt like a dragon at Fan and Han and struck like lightning at Xiang and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He said Zhou could be punished; without expecting it they assembled; he leapt like a dragon at Fan and Han and struck like lightning at Xiang and Ying.

sentences.zh: 翦離德如振槁，取獨夫如拾遺，其雄才大略，固無得而稱矣。

translations.literal: Cutting off the virtue of Li was like shaking dry stalks; taking the lone tyrant was like picking up what was lost—his heroic talent and great design truly cannot be fully praised.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting off the virtue of Li was like shaking dry stalks; taking the lone tyrant was like picking up what was lost—his heroic talent and great design truly cannot be fully praised.

sentences.zh: 既縣白旗之首，方應皇天之眷，布德施惠，悅近來遠。

translations.literal: Already he had hung the head on the white flag; then he answered Heaven's favor; he spread virtue and showed grace, pleasing the near and reaching the far.
translations.idiomatic: Already he had hung the head on the white flag; then he answered Heaven's favor; he spread virtue and showed grace, pleasing the near and reaching the far.

sentences.zh: 開蕩蕩之王道，革靡靡之商俗。

translations.literal: He opened the broad Way of kings and reformed the decadent customs of Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the broad Way of kings and reformed the decadent customs of Shang.

sentences.zh: 大修文教，盛飾禮容，鼓扇玄風，闡揚儒業。

translations.literal: He greatly cultivated wen and education, richly adorned ritual and bearing, stirred the mysterious wind, and exalted Confucian enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly cultivated wen and education, richly adorned ritual and bearing, stirred the mysterious wind, and exalted Confucian enterprise.

sentences.zh: 介胄仁義，折沖尊俎，聲振寰宇，澤流遐裔，干戈載戢，凡數十年，濟濟焉，洋洋焉，魏、晉以來，未有若斯之盛也。

translations.literal: Armor wore benevolence and righteousness; he overturned the enemy at the banquet table; his fame shook the realm and his grace flowed to distant lands; weapons were laid aside for several decades—vast and abundant, since Wei and Jin there had been nothing like this splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Armor wore benevolence and righteousness; he overturned the enemy at the banquet table; his fame shook the realm and his grace flowed to distant lands; weapons were laid aside for several decades—vast and abundant, since Wei and Jin there had been nothing like this splendor.

sentences.zh: 然不能息末敦本，斲雕為樸，慕名好事，崇尚浮華，抑揚孔、墨，流連釋、老。

translations.literal: Yet he could not rest the branch and strengthen the root, carve away ornament and return to simplicity; he admired reputation and loved novelty and honored the floating and splendid; he elevated and suppressed Confucius and Mozi and lingered over Buddhism and Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not rest the branch and strengthen the root, carve away ornament and return to simplicity; he admired reputation and loved novelty and honored the floating and splendid; he elevated and suppressed Confucius and Mozi and lingered over Buddhism and Daoism.

sentences.zh: 或終夜不寢，或日旰不食，非弘道以利物，惟飾智以驚愚。

translations.literal: Sometimes he did not sleep the whole night; sometimes he did not eat until the sun set—not to broaden the Way to benefit things, but only to adorn wisdom and startle fools.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he did not sleep the whole night; sometimes he did not eat until the sun set—not to broaden the Way to benefit things, but only to adorn wisdom and startle fools.

sentences.zh: 且心未遺榮，虛廁蒼頭之伍，高談脫屣，終戀黃屋之尊。

translations.literal: Moreover his heart had not left glory; he vainly sat among the ranks of menials; he talked loftily of casting off the world yet to the end cherished the honor of the yellow canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his heart had not left glory; he vainly sat among the ranks of menials; he talked loftily of casting off the world yet to the end cherished the honor of the yellow canopy.

sentences.zh: 夫人之大欲，在乎飲食男女，至於軒冕殿堂，非有切身之急。

translations.literal: The great desires of man lie in food, drink, and the relations of men and women; as for carriages, caps, halls, and palaces—there is no urgent need touching the person.
translations.idiomatic: The great desires of man lie in food, drink, and the relations of men and women; as for carriages, caps, halls, and palaces—there is no urgent need touching the person.

sentences.zh: 高祖屏除嗜欲，眷戀軒冕，得其所難，而滯于所易，可謂神有所不達，智有所不通矣。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor screened out appetites yet clung to carriages and caps; he obtained what is hard yet stalled at what is easy—this may be called spirit not reaching everywhere and wisdom not penetrating all.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor screened out appetites yet clung to carriages and caps; he obtained what is hard yet stalled at what is easy—this may be called spirit not reaching everywhere and wisdom not penetrating all.

sentences.zh: 逮夫精華稍竭，鳳德已衰，惑於聽受，權在奸佞，儲後百辟，莫能盡言。

translations.literal: When his essence and splendor gradually failed and phoenix virtue had declined, he was deluded in what he heard and power lay with wicked flatterers; the heir and the hundred officials—none could speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: When his essence and splendor gradually failed and phoenix virtue had declined, he was deluded in what he heard and power lay with wicked flatterers; the heir and the hundred officials—none could speak fully.

sentences.zh: 險躁之心，暮年逾甚，見利而動，愎諫違卜。

translations.literal: His rash and restless heart grew worse in old age; seeing profit he moved; stubbornly he rejected remonstrance and defied divination.
translations.idiomatic: His rash and restless heart grew worse in old age; seeing profit he moved; stubbornly he rejected remonstrance and defied divination.

sentences.zh: 開門揖盜，棄好即讎，釁起蕭牆，禍成戎、羯，身殞非命，災被億兆。

translations.literal: He opened the gate to welcome robbers, abandoned friendship and turned to enmity; the provocation arose within the palace wall; calamity was completed by the Rong and Jie; he died an unnatural death and disaster struck hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the gate to welcome robbers, abandoned friendship and turned to enmity; the provocation arose within the palace wall; calamity was completed by the Rong and Jie; he died an unnatural death and disaster struck hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 衣冠斃鋒鏑之下，老幼粉戎馬之足，瞻彼黍離，痛深周廟；

translations.literal: Gentlemen and officials perished under blade and arrow; old and young were ground beneath the hooves of war horses; gazing at that millet in ruin, the pain exceeded the Zhou temple;
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen and officials perished under blade and arrow; old and young were ground beneath the hooves of war horses; gazing at that millet in ruin, the pain exceeded the Zhou temple;

sentences.zh: 永言麥秀，悲甚殷墟。

translations.literal: forever speaking of the wheat in ear, the grief exceeded the ruins of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: forever speaking of the wheat in ear, the grief exceeded the ruins of Yin.

sentences.zh: 自古以安為危，既成而敗，顛覆之速，書契所未聞也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, taking peace as peril and success as failure—the speed of overturning is unheard of in written records.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, taking peace as peril and success as failure—the speed of overturning is unheard of in written records.

sentences.zh: 易曰：「天之所助者順，人之所助者信。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "Heaven helps the obedient; men help the faithful."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "Heaven helps the obedient; men help the faithful."

sentences.zh: 」高祖之遇斯屯剝，不得其死，蓋動而之險，不由信順，失天人之助，其能免於此乎。

translations.literal: That the High Ancestor met this time of hardship and stripping and did not obtain natural death—surely because in movement he went toward peril and did not follow faith and obedience; losing Heaven's and men's help, how could he escape this?
translations.idiomatic: That the High Ancestor met this time of hardship and stripping and did not obtain natural death—surely because in movement he went toward peril and did not follow faith and obedience; losing Heaven's and men's help, how could he escape this?

sentences.zh: 太宗敏叡過人，神采秀髮，多聞博達，富贍詞藻。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was keen and surpassing in men, with spirit and appearance splendidly flourishing; he heard much, reached far, and was rich and ample in literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was keen and surpassing in men, with spirit and appearance splendidly flourishing; he heard much, reached far, and was rich and ample in literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 然文豔用寡，華而不實，體窮淫麗，義罕疏通，哀思之音，遂移風俗，以此而貞萬國，異乎周誦、漢莊矣。

translations.literal: Yet his writing was brilliant but his use sparse, flowery but not solid; his style exhausted licentious beauty and his meaning rarely penetrated; the tone of mournful longing shifted custom—by this to hold the myriad states differs from King Song of Zhou and Emperor Zhuang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his writing was brilliant but his use sparse, flowery but not solid; his style exhausted licentious beauty and his meaning rarely penetrated; the tone of mournful longing shifted custom—by this to hold the myriad states differs from King Song of Zhou and Emperor Zhuang of Han.

sentences.zh: 我生不辰，載離多難，桀逆構扇，巨猾滔天，始同牖裏之拘，終類望夷之禍，悠悠蒼昊，其可問哉。

translations.literal: I was born at the wrong time and repeatedly parted from peace; the cruel rebel constructed turmoil and the great villain flooded Heaven—I began like one confined in the windowed room and ended like the calamity at Wangyi; vast blue Heaven—can it be questioned?
translations.idiomatic: I was born at the wrong time and repeatedly parted from peace; the cruel rebel constructed turmoil and the great villain flooded Heaven—I began like one confined in the windowed room and ended like the calamity at Wangyi; vast blue Heaven—can it be questioned?

sentences.zh: 昔國步初屯，兵纏魏闕，群後釋位，投袂勤王。

translations.literal: Formerly when the nation's step first faltered, war entangled the Wei gate; the feudal lords released their posts and rolled up their sleeves to serve the king.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when the nation's step first faltered, war entangled the Wei gate; the feudal lords released their posts and rolled up their sleeves to serve the king.

sentences.zh: 元帝以磐石之宗，受分陝之任，屬君親之難，居連率之長，不能撫劍嘗膽，枕戈泣血，躬先士卒，致命前驅。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan as a foundation stone of the clan received the charge of dividing Shaan; facing the ruler's and parent's calamity, he held the post of regional commander—yet he could not grasp the sword and taste gall, pillow the spear and weep blood, take the lead among soldiers and stake his life in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan as a foundation stone of the clan received the charge of dividing Shaan; facing the ruler's and parent's calamity, he held the post of regional commander—yet he could not grasp the sword and taste gall, pillow the spear and weep blood, take the lead among soldiers and stake his life in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 遂乃擁眾逡巡，內懷觖望，坐觀國變，以為身幸。

translations.literal: He then held the host yet hesitated, inwardly harbored divided hopes, sat watching the nation's change and took it as personal fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He then held the host yet hesitated, inwardly harbored divided hopes, sat watching the nation's change and took it as personal fortune.

sentences.zh: 不急莽、卓之誅，先行昆弟之戮。

translations.literal: He did not urgently seek the punishment of Wang Mang and Zhuo—first he carried out the slaughter of brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He did not urgently seek the punishment of Wang Mang and Zhuo—first he carried out the slaughter of brothers.

sentences.zh: 又沈猜忍酷，多行無禮，騁智辯以飾非，肆忿戾以害物，爪牙重將，心膂謀臣，或顧眄以就拘囚，或一言而及葅醢，朝之君子，相顧懍然。

translations.literal: Again he was deep in suspicion, cruel, and ruthless, often acting without propriety; he deployed clever debate to cover wrong and unleashed wrath and harshness to harm people; trusted generals and ministers of heart and spine—some were seized with a glance, some reached minced pickle with a single word; the gentlemen of the court looked at one another in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was deep in suspicion, cruel, and ruthless, often acting without propriety; he deployed clever debate to cover wrong and unleashed wrath and harshness to harm people; trusted generals and ministers of heart and spine—some were seized with a glance, some reached minced pickle with a single word; the gentlemen of the court looked at one another in fear.

sentences.zh: 自謂安若泰山，算無遺策，怵於邪說，即安荊楚。

translations.literal: He thought himself secure as Mount Tai, his calculations without omission; deluded by perverse counsel, he then settled in Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He thought himself secure as Mount Tai, his calculations without omission; deluded by perverse counsel, he then settled in Jing and Chu.

sentences.zh: 雖元惡克翦，社稷未寧，而西鄰責言，禍敗旋及，斯乃上靈降鑒，此焉假手，天道人事，其可誣乎。

translations.literal: Though the great villain was cut down and the altars were not yet at peace, the western neighbor reproached him and disaster and defeat soon followed—this was the upper spirit lowering inspection and lending its hand here; Heaven's Way and human affairs—how can they be deceived?
translations.idiomatic: Though the great villain was cut down and the altars were not yet at peace, the western neighbor reproached him and disaster and defeat soon followed—this was the upper spirit lowering inspection and lending its hand here; Heaven's Way and human affairs—how can they be deceived?

sentences.zh: 其篤志藝文，采浮華而棄忠信，戎昭果毅，先骨肉而後寇讎。

translations.literal: His steadfast will in arts and letters gathered the floating and splendid and cast aside loyalty and faith; in martial proclamation he was resolute and bold—first against kin, then against enemies.
translations.idiomatic: His steadfast will in arts and letters gathered the floating and splendid and cast aside loyalty and faith; in martial proclamation he was resolute and bold—first against kin, then against enemies.

sentences.zh: 口誦六經，心通百氏，有仲尼之學，有公旦之才，適足以益其驕矜，增其禍患，何補金陵之覆沒 ，何救江陵之滅亡哉！

translations.literal: His mouth recited the Six Classics and his heart penetrated the hundred schools; he had the learning of Confucius and the talent of the Duke of Zhou—yet it only increased his pride and added to his calamities; what did it remedy the fall of Jinling, what did it save the extinction of Jiangling!
translations.idiomatic: His mouth recited the Six Classics and his heart penetrated the hundred schools; he had the learning of Confucius and the talent of the Duke of Zhou—yet it only increased his pride and added to his calamities; what did it remedy the fall of Jinling, what did it save the extinction of Jiangling!

sentences.zh: 敬帝遭家不造，紹茲屯運，征伐有所自出，政刑不由於己。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing met with an unpropitious house and inherited this time of hardship; campaigns issued from elsewhere and government and punishment were not in his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing met with an unpropitious house and inherited this time of hardship; campaigns issued from elsewhere and government and punishment were not in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 時無伊、霍之輔，焉得不為高讓歟。

translations.literal: At the time there were no Yi and Huo to assist him—how could he not yield the throne high?
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were no Yi and Huo to assist him—how could he not yield the throne high?
